The earth will be swept totally empty and stripped of everything,
because Yahweh has said so.

The earth dries up and mourns.
The world droops and fades.
The greatest people on earth droop too.

The earth is spoiled by those who live on it,
because they broke the laws,
ignored the rules,
and shattered the lasting agreement.{b}

So a curse eats up the earth,
and its people must pay for their guilt.
Those who live on earth burn up,
and only a few are left alive.

The new wine is gone, and the vines wilt.
All the merrymakers groan.

The happy sound of tambourines has stopped.
The noise of the partying has ended.
The cheerful harp is silent.

No one drinks wine while singing.
Strong drink tastes bitter to those who sip it.

The city of confusion lies in pieces.
Each house is barred shut, so no one can enter.{c}

People cry in the streets for wine.
All joy has turned to gloom.
The happiness of the land has gone away.

Only ruin is left in the city,
and its gate is smashed to bits.

This is how it will be everywhere on earth and among the nations,
like when olive trees are beaten,
like the few grapes left when the harvest is over.

Some raise their voices and sing for joy.
From the west they shout about the greatness of Yahweh.{d}

So in the east, give honor to Yahweh.
On the seacoasts, praise the name of Yahweh, the God of Israel.{e}

From the farthest corners of the earth we hear singing:
“Glory belongs to the Righteous One!”
But I said, “I am fading away! I am fading away! Woe to me!
Traitors betray,
and traitors keep on betraying.”{f}

Terror, pit, and trap
wait for you who live on earth.{g}

Whoever flees at the sound of terror will drop into the pit.
Whoever scrambles out of the pit will be snared by the trap.
The floodgates of the sky burst open,
and the earth’s foundations rock.

The earth is split open.
The earth is torn apart.
The earth is shaken to pieces.

The earth lurches like a drunkard.
It rocks like a shack in the wind.
Its rebellion is a heavy weight on it.
It falls and will not stand up again.{h}

On that day Yahweh will punish the powers in heaven
and the kings on earth.

Then the moon will blush, and the sun will be ashamed,
because Yahweh of Armies will be King
on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem,
and his elders will see his glory.{j}

notes.text: Or “the land.” The same Hebrew word means earth or land.
Or “covenant.”
Or “city of emptiness.”
Or “from the sea.”
Or “in the islands of the sea.”
The meaning of “wasting away” (Hebrew raz) is uncertain. “Righteous One” can also be “the righteous.”
There is a word play in Hebrew: pachad, pachath, pach (“terror, pit, trap”).
Or “and will not rise.” Compare Amos 5:2.
Or “they will be visited.” The Hebrew can also mean “they will be remembered.”
Or “and before his elders there will be glory.”

verses.text:
You turned a city into a pile of rocks,
a walled town into ruins.
The foreigners’ fortress is no city anymore,
and it will never be rebuilt.

So strong peoples will honor you,
and cities of cruel nations will fear you.

You were a safe place for the weak,
a safe place for the poor in their need,
shelter from the storm and shade from the heat,
when the blast of the cruel is like a rainstorm beating on a wall

or like heat in dry land.
You silence the noise of the foreigners.
As a cloud’s shade cools the heat,
the song of the cruel dies down.

On this mountain Yahweh of Armies will serve
a banquet for every nation,
with the finest food and aged wine,
tender meat full of marrow,
and wine strained until it sparkles.{b}

He will swallow up death for good.
The Lord Yahweh will wipe away the tears from every face.
He will take his people’s shame off the whole earth.
Yahweh himself has said so.{d}

When that day comes, they will say,
“This is our God!
We hoped in him, and he rescued us.
This is Yahweh. We hoped in him.
Let us shout with delight at the rescue he brings.”{e}

Moab will thrash its arms in the middle of the pit,
as a swimmer thrashes to swim,
but Yahweh will crush its pride
and the skill of its hands.{g}

He will bring down your high, walled fortress.
He will throw it down and make it hit the ground, the very dust.

notes.text: Some ancient copies read a little differently.
The meat is described as “fat with marrow” and the wine as “refined.”
Or “the shroud.”
Paul quotes the first line in 1 Corinthians 15:54, and Revelation 7:17 and 21:4 echo the second line.
Or “Look, this is our God, whom we waited for to save us.”
Moab was the kingdom east of the Dead Sea. See 15:1. “Manure pit” is Hebrew madmenah, as in 10:31.
The Hebrew words for “tricks” are uncertain.

verses.text:
Open the gates
so the good nation that stays faithful can come in.{b}

Trust Yahweh always,
for in Yah, Yahweh, we have a rock that lasts forever.{d}

He knocked down those who lived on the heights,
the city that rose so high.
He levels it, levels it to the earth
and drops it in the dirt.

Feet walk on it,
the feet of the poor,
the steps of the needy.”

The road of good people is smooth.
You, the Upright One, make their path level.{e}

Yes, Yahweh, we wait for you
as your judgments come.
Our deepest wish
is for your name and for the memory of you.{f}

My soul longs for you in the night.
My spirit inside me searches for you at dawn.
When your judgments fall on the earth,
the world’s people learn what is right.

Even when kindness is shown to the wicked,
they do not learn what is right.
In a land of honest people they still do wrong,
and they ignore Yahweh’s greatness.

Yahweh, you are the one who brings us peace.
All that we have achieved, you achieved for us.

Yahweh our God,
other lords besides you have ruled over us,
yet your name alone is the one we honor.

The dead stay dead.
Ghosts do not get up.
You came, you wiped them out,
and you erased all memory of them.{h}

You made the nation larger, Yahweh.
You made the nation larger and showed your glory.
You pushed back all the borders of the land.

Like a pregnant woman near her time
who twists and screams in labor,
that is how we were in your presence, Yahweh.

We were pregnant and twisted in pain,
but all we gave birth to was wind.
We did not bring rescue to the land,
and no new people were born into the world.{j}

But your dead will live. Their bodies will rise.
Wake up and sing for joy, you who lie in the dust!
Your dew is like the dew at dawn,
and the earth will give birth to those who have died.{k}

Come, my people, step into your rooms
and close the doors after you.
Stay hidden for a brief moment
until his fury has passed by.{l}

Look! Yahweh steps out from where he lives
to punish earth’s people for their guilt.
The ground will uncover the blood soaked into it
and no longer hide those killed on it.

notes.text: Or “He sets up rescue as walls and ramparts.”
Or “that keeps truth.”
Or “a mind that leans on you.” The Hebrew can also be read “the mind that is firm.”
Yah is a short form of Yahweh. “Rock” is Hebrew tsur ‘olamim, “rock of the ages.”
Or “the Straight One.”
Or “the path of your judgments.”
Or “let the fire for your enemies eat them.” The Hebrew is uncertain.
Hebrew repha’im, the ghosts or shades of the dead. This verse speaks of those other masters.
Hebrew “they poured out a whisper (or a charm).” The meaning is uncertain.
Or “no one fell into the world,” or “the people of the world were not born.”
Or “and the earth will give birth to the shades.” The Great Isaiah Scroll adds “my corpses will rise.”
Hebrew “chambers.”

verses.text: On that day Yahweh will use his mighty, powerful sword to punish Leviathan, the fast-moving snake. He will punish Leviathan, the coiling snake, and he will kill the sea dragon.{a}

On that day:
“Sing about a vineyard that makes fine wine.{b}

I, Yahweh, am the one who tends it.
I water it every moment.
So no one can harm it,
I stand guard over it day and night.

I am not angry.
If only I had thorn bushes and weeds to deal with!
I would march into battle against them
and burn them all up together.{c}

Or else let them grab hold of my strength
and make peace with me.
Yes, let them make peace with me.”

In the days ahead Jacob will take root.
Israel will bud and bloom,
and fill the world’s surface with fruit.

Did Yahweh hit Israel as hard as he hit those who hit Israel?
Or was Israel killed the way Israel’s killers were killed?

By sending her away, little by little, you argued with her.
He drove her out with his harsh wind, when the east wind blew.{d}

This is how Jacob’s guilt will be forgiven,
and this is the whole reward for taking away his sin:
he will crush every altar stone
like chalk ground into powder.
Not one Asherah pole or incense stand will be left standing.{e}

The fortified city is empty,
a deserted place left like the desert.
Calves graze there and lie down there,
and they strip the branches bare.

When the branches dry up, they snap off.
Women come and use them for firewood.
These are people who do not understand.
So the one who made them will not pity them,
and the one who shaped them will not be kind to them.
On that day Yahweh will beat out the grain from the River’s flow to the Brook of Egypt, and you Israelites will be picked up one at a time.{f}
When that day comes, a huge trumpet will blast. Those who were lost in Assyria and those scattered in Egypt will come and bow down to Yahweh on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.{g}

notes.text: Leviathan means “coiled one.” It is a sea monster in old stories (compare Psalm 74:14 and Job 41).
Some ancient copies read a little differently. The Hebrew word is uncertain.
Or “Who will give me thorns and weeds in battle? I would march against them.”
The Hebrew of verses 7-8 is hard, and the meaning is uncertain.
Asherah poles were wooden pillars or trees linked to the goddess Asherah.
The River is the Euphrates. The Brook of Egypt is the Wadi el-Arish, the border between Egypt and Canaan.
Assyria and Egypt may stand for all the lands where exiles were scattered.

verses.text:
Shame on the proud wreath of Ephraim’s drunks,
on the fading flower of its lovely beauty.
It sits on the head of a rich valley
full of people knocked down by wine.{a}

Watch! The Lord has a powerful, mighty agent.
He is like a hailstorm or a wrecking wind,
like a flood of heavy, pouring water.
With one hand he slams the wreath to the ground.{b}

The proud wreath of Ephraim’s drunks
will be stomped under foot.

The fading flower of its lovely beauty,
sitting on the head of a rich valley,
will be like a fig that ripens before summer.
Whoever spots it grabs it
and gulps it down before it leaves his palm.

On that day Yahweh of Armies will be a glorious wreath,
a beautiful crown
for those of his people who are left.

He will give a sense of justice to the one who judges,
and strength to those who fight off attackers at the gate.

But these men also reel from wine
and wander off course because of strong drink.
Priest and prophet both stagger from liquor.
Wine makes them foggy,
and strong drink makes them wobble.
They stumble when they see visions
and trip when they decide cases.

Every table is covered with vomit and filth,
with no clean spot anywhere.

They say, “Who does he think he is teaching?
Who is he explaining his message to?
Babies just off milk?
Children just taken from the breast?

Very well, then. Through foreign lips and a strange language
he will speak to these people.{d}

God once told them,
“Here is where to rest. Give the exhausted a place to rest.
Here is where it is calm.”
But they refused to hear it.

So Yahweh’s word to them will be
“tsav latsav, tsav latsav,
qav laqav, qav laqav,
a little here, a little there.”
They will walk on, fall backward,
get hurt, get trapped, and be taken away.

So listen to Yahweh’s word, you mockers
who rule these people in Jerusalem.

You have said, “We made a deal with death.
We signed an agreement with the grave.
When the flooding whip sweeps past,
it will not touch us.
We made lies our shelter
and hid behind falsehood.”{e}

So the Lord Yahweh says:
“Watch, I am setting down a stone in Zion as the foundation.
It is a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a firm base.
Whoever trusts in it will not panic.{f}

I will make justice the measuring line
and right living the weight that hangs from it.
Hail will sweep away your shelter of lies,
and water will flood your hiding place.

Your deal with death will be wiped out.
Your pact with the grave will not hold.
When the flooding whip sweeps past,
it will trample you down.

Each time it sweeps by, it will carry you off.
It will come through every morning,
in the daytime and at night.
Just understanding the report will bring terror.”{g}

The bed is too short to stretch out on,
and the blanket is too narrow to wrap around you.

So stop mocking,
or your chains will get stronger.
I have heard the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, announce
the destruction of the whole land.{i}

Lean in and hear my voice.
Pay attention and hear what I say.

Does a farmer plow all day long just to plant?
Does he keep breaking up and raking the soil?

After he has smoothed the ground,
does he not scatter dill and sprinkle cumin,
put wheat in rows,
barley in its own plot,
and spelt around the edge?{j}

His God teaches him the right way.
He gives him the know-how.

Dill is not threshed with a heavy sledge,
and a cart wheel is not rolled over cumin.
Dill is beaten out with a stick,
and cumin with a rod.

Grain for bread has to be ground,
but no one threshes it forever.
He drives his cart wheel and horses over it,
but he does not crush it to powder.{k}

notes.text: Ephraim means “doubly fruitful.” It stands for the northern kingdom, whose capital was Samaria on a hill over a rich valley.
Hebrew “the Lord has one strong and mighty.” This may mean the king of Assyria.
The Hebrew sounds are tsav latsav and qav laqav. They may be baby talk or a mocking copy of the prophet’s teaching, like “rule on rule, line on line.” Compare verse 13.
Paul quotes this verse in 1 Corinthians 14:21. The foreign language is probably Assyrian.
Sheol is the place of the dead. “Flooding whip” is a picture of the invading army.
1 Peter 2:6 and Romans 9:33 quote this verse from the Septuagint. Some ancient copies read a little differently.
Or “to hear the report.”
Mount Perazim and Gibeon were places where Yahweh beat the Philistines for David (2 Samuel 5:20-25).
Or “decreed destruction.”
Dill, cumin, and spelt were common crops. Hebrew nisman for “its border” is uncertain.
The Hebrew is hard in verses 25-28, and some words are rare.
Hebrew “great in wise help (tushiyyah).”

verses.text:
Shame on you, Ariel, Ariel,
the city where David set up camp!
Add one year to another.
Let the festivals go around in their cycle.{a}

You will sink low and talk from the ground.
Your words will be faint, rising from the dust.
You will sound like a spirit under the earth,
and your talk will whisper up out of the dirt.

Yahweh of Armies will come to you
with thunder, an earthquake, and a great noise,
with a windstorm, a hurricane,
and flames of a fire that eats everything.

Think of a starving man dreaming.
He sees himself eating,
but he wakes up with an empty stomach.
Think of a parched man dreaming.
He sees himself drinking,
but he wakes up weak,
still dry and longing for water.
That is how it will be for the crowd of all nations
who fight against Mount Zion.

Stop and stare in shock.
Shut your eyes and be blind.
You are drunk, but not from wine.
You wobble, but not from liquor.{f}
The whole vision is to you like the words of a scroll that has been sealed. When someone hands it to a reader and asks, “Read this out, please,” the answer is, “I can’t. It has a seal on it.”
And when someone hands the scroll to a person who never learned to read and asks, “Read this out, please,” the answer is, “I don’t know how to read.”

The Lord said:
“These people come close with their mouths.
They honor me with their lips,
but their hearts are far from me.
Their respect for me is only a rule that people taught them.{h}

So once again I will do astonishing things to these people,
amazing things beyond belief.
The wisdom of their wise men will disappear,
and the understanding of their clever men will vanish.”{i}

Shame on those who dig deep to keep their plans from Yahweh,
who do their deeds in the dark,
and who ask, “Who is watching? Who will find out?”

What a twisted way to think!
Should a potter be treated like his clay?
Can something that was made tell its maker, “You never made me”?
Can a pot say of its shaper, “He has no idea what he is doing”?{j}

On that day deaf people will hear a scroll being read.
Blind eyes will see
out of the gloom and the dark.

The poor will be glad again in Yahweh.
The neediest people will cheer for the Holy One of Israel.

The cruel will disappear, and the mockers will be gone.
Everyone who looks for a chance to do wrong will be cut down.

So this is what Yahweh, who bought Abraham back, says about Jacob’s family:
“Jacob will not be ashamed anymore.
His face will not turn white with fear anymore.

When he sees his children,
the work of my hands, among his people,
they will honor my name as holy.
They will honor the Holy One of Jacob as holy
and stand in awe of the God of Israel.

People who wandered in spirit will gain understanding,
and complainers will accept correction.”

notes.text: Ariel may mean “lion of God” or “altar hearth.” It is a name for Jerusalem, where David camped.
Hebrew ‘ari’el, which is also the word for an altar’s hearth (Ezekiel 43:15).
The Great Isaiah Scroll and the Septuagint say “like David” (“I will camp against you as David did”).
The Septuagint reads “the crowd of the ungodly” in place of “ruthless attackers.”
Hebrew “like a dream, a vision of the night.”
Or “Be amazed and astonished.”
Some ancient copies read a little differently.
Jesus quotes verse 13 in Matthew 15:8-9 and Mark 7:6-7, following the Septuagint.
Paul quotes this in 1 Corinthians 1:19 from the Septuagint.
Compare Romans 9:20.
Or “will become a fruit orchard, and the orchard will be counted as a forest.”
Some ancient copies read a little differently.

verses.text:
“Shame on my stubborn children,” says Yahweh.
“They follow plans I did not make.
They sign treaties my Spirit did not start,
and so they pile sin on sin.{a}

They set off for Egypt
without asking me.
They take refuge in Pharaoh’s strength
and hide in Egypt’s shade.

But Pharaoh’s strength will bring you shame,
and hiding in Egypt’s shade will leave you confused.

His rulers are in Zoan,
and his envoys have arrived in Hanes.{b}

All of them will be ashamed
of a people who cannot help them.
They bring no aid and no gain,
only shame and disgrace.”

Here is a word about the animals of the Negev.
Through a land of hardship and trouble,
of lions, both male and female,
of vipers and flying, fiery snakes,
they carry their riches on donkeys’ backs
and their treasure on camels’ humps,
to give to a nation that cannot help them.{c}

Now go, write it down in front of them on a tablet.
Put it in a book
so it will last for days to come
as a witness forever.{e}

These are rebellious people, children who lie,
children who refuse to hear Yahweh’s teaching.{f}

They tell the seers, “Do not see!”
They tell the prophets, “Do not give us true visions!
Tell us pleasant things.
See fantasies for us.

Get off the road. Leave the path.
Do not mention the Holy One of Israel to us anymore.”

So this is what the Holy One of Israel says:
“You hate this message.
You trust in cruelty and crooked dealing
and lean on them.

So this sin will be for you
like a crack in a high wall,
bulging out and ready to fall.
It will crash down suddenly, in an instant.

He will smash it like a clay jar,
broken without mercy,
so that among the pieces
not one piece is big enough to carry coals from a fire
or scoop water from a pool.”

The Lord Yahweh, the Holy One of Israel, says this:
“You would be saved by coming back and by resting.
Calm and trust would make you strong.”
But you refused.

You said, “No, we will gallop away on horses!”
So you will gallop away.
You said, “We will ride swift mounts!”
So the ones chasing you will be swift too.

A thousand of you will run from one man’s threat.
From five men’s threat, all of you will run,
until you are left like a lone pole on a mountaintop,
like a signal flag on a hill.

Yet Yahweh is waiting to be kind to you.
He will stand up to have pity on you.
Yahweh is a God of fairness.
Happy are all who wait for him.{g}

People will live in Zion, in Jerusalem.
You will not cry anymore.
When you cry for help, he will be kind, no doubt.
The moment he hears you, he will answer.{h}

The Lord may give you the bread of trouble
and the water of pain,
but your Teacher will not hide anymore.
Your own eyes will see your Teacher.{i}

Whether you veer to the right or to the left,
a voice behind you will say,
“Here is the road. Walk along it.”

You will call your silver-covered statues unclean,
and your gold-plated idols too.
You will toss them away like soiled rags.
You will tell them, “Get out!”

He will send rain on the seed you plant in the field.
The food that grows from the soil
will be rich and plentiful.
When that day comes, your cattle will graze in roomy pastures.

The oxen and young donkeys that work the soil
will eat seasoned feed,
sifted with a shovel and a fork.

On every high mountain and every tall hill
there will be streams of flowing water.
That will happen on the day of the great slaughter, when towers fall.

The moon will glow like the sun,
and the sun will blaze seven times as bright,
like the light of seven days all at once,
on the day Yahweh bandages his people’s broken places
and heals the wounds his blows left.

Look, Yahweh’s name comes from far away,
burning with his anger, with thick rising smoke.
His lips are full of rage,
and his tongue is like a fire that eats everything.{j}

His breath is like a flooding river
that climbs to the neck.
He sifts the nations in a net of ruin,
and he fits a bridle in the jaws of peoples to steer them off course.

You will have a song like the one on the night of a holy feast.
You will have joy in your heart, like a person walking with a flute
to the mountain of Yahweh, to Israel’s Rock.

Yahweh will make his powerful voice heard.
He will show his arm coming down in a blow,
with furious anger and flames that eat everything,
with a cloudburst, a storm, and hailstones.

Yahweh’s voice will shatter Assyria
when he strikes with his rod.

Every blow of the staff he has chosen,
which Yahweh lays on Assyria,
will land to the sound of tambourines and harps.
He will fight them in battles with his arm swinging.{k}

A burning place called Topheth was set up long ago.
It is ready for the king too.
Its fire pit is deep and wide,
with plenty of fire and wood.
Yahweh’s breath, like a stream of burning sulfur, lights it.{l}

notes.text: Or “who pour out a drink offering (make a treaty) but not by my Spirit.” The Hebrew can mean making an agreement.
Zoan was a delta city in Egypt. Hanes (Hebrew Hanes) was probably Heracleopolis, south of the delta.
“Message” is Hebrew massa’. The Negev is the dry south of Judah.
Rahab is a name for a sea monster in old stories and is used here as a name for Egypt (compare Psalm 87:4). Hebrew “Rahab, they sit still” (or “Rahab who does nothing”).
Some ancient copies read a little differently.
Or “instruction” (Hebrew torah).
Or “Yahweh waits so that he may be kind.”
Or “he will answer you.”
Or “your teachers,” with a plural noun. The Hebrew can mean either.
Hebrew “the name of Yahweh.” It means Yahweh himself.
Hebrew “battles of waving,” a picture of his swinging arm. Some ancient copies read a little differently.
Topheth was the fire place in the Hinnom Valley where children were burned in sacrifice (2 Kings 23:10). “The king” may be Assyria’s king, or it may be “Molech” (compare Leviticus 18:21).

subheads.8: A People Who Will Not Listen

verses.text:
Shame on those who go down to Egypt for help,
who rely on horses
and trust in huge numbers of chariots
and in the great strength of riders,
but never look to the Holy One of Israel
or ask Yahweh for advice!

Yet he too is wise, and he can send disaster.
He does not take back what he says.
He will stand against the family of evildoers
and against those who help the wicked.

The Egyptians are human beings, not God.
Their horses are flesh, not spirit.
When Yahweh stretches out his hand,
the helper will trip, and the one who was helped will fall.
They will all be finished together.{a}

This is what Yahweh told me:
“A lion growls over his kill.
Even a whole group of shepherds called to fight him
cannot scare him with their shouts,
or frighten him with their noise.
In the same way Yahweh of Armies will come down
to fight on Mount Zion and its hill.

Like birds flying over a nest,
Yahweh of Armies will protect Jerusalem.
He will protect it and save it.
He will spare it and rescue it.”{b}
Return to the one Israel has turned so far against.{c}
On that day every person will throw away the silver idols and gold idols that their own hands made for them, and that led them to sin.

“Assyria will fall by a sword that is not a man’s.
A sword that is not a human’s will eat him up.
He will run from the sword,
and his young men will be put to forced work.{d}

His rock will pass away in terror,
and his officers will panic at the sight of the flag,”
says Yahweh, whose fire burns in Zion
and whose furnace burns in Jerusalem.{e}

notes.text: The Egyptians were seen as a strong force with many horses and chariots.
“Spare” translates the Hebrew word for “pass over,” like Passover (Exodus 12:13).
Or “Come back to him against whom the people of Israel have so deeply rebelled.”
The Hebrew can also be “will not be a man’s sword.” Forced work is hard labor for a conqueror.
“His rock” may mean the Assyrian king’s fortress or his god.

verses.text:
A king will rule with what is right,
and his officials will govern with fairness.

Each of them will be a windbreak,
a cover from the storm,
like streams running through dry ground,
like the shade of a huge rock in a worn-out land.

Eyes that can see will no longer be shut,
and ears that can hear will listen.

The hasty mind will learn to understand,
and stammering tongues will speak clearly and quickly.

No one will call a fool a noble anymore,
or praise a crook as a generous man.{a}

A fool says foolish things,
and his mind plans wrong.
He lives without God
and tells lies about Yahweh.
He leaves the hungry with nothing to eat
and keeps drink from the thirsty.{b}

A crook uses evil tools.
He dreams up wicked schemes
to ruin poor people with lies,
even when the needy person is telling the truth.

But a generous man plans generous things,
and his generous acts keep him standing.

Get up, you women who live in comfort, and listen to me.
You women who feel so safe, hear what I say.

In a little over a year
you who feel safe will shudder,
because the grape crop will fail
and no harvest will come in.{c}

Tremble, you women who are comfortable.
Shake with worry, you who do not care.
Take off your clothes and stand bare,
and tie sackcloth around your waists.{d}

They beat their chests
over the lovely fields and the fruitful vines,

over the soil of my people
that grows thorns and weeds,
and over every happy home in the town that was so full of fun.

The palace will be left empty,
and the loud city will be deserted.
The hill and the watchtower
will turn into caves for good,
a happy place for wild donkeys and a pasture for flocks.{e}

This will last until the Spirit is poured on us from heaven,
the wilderness turns into an orchard,
and the orchard is thought of as a forest.

Then justice will live in the desert,
and right living will settle in the fertile field.

The result of right living will be peace.
Its effect will be calm and safety that last forever.

My people will live in a peaceful home,
in safe houses and quiet places to rest.

Even if hail comes down on the forest as it falls,
and the city is flattened completely,{f}

you will be happy, you who plant seed beside every stream
and let your ox and donkey wander free.

notes.text: The Hebrew words for “fool” (nabal) and “crook” (kilay) are stock names for the selfish and the wicked.
Or “to leave the soul of the hungry empty.” Compare Job 22:7.
Hebrew “days over a year.” Some read “a year and some days.”
Hebrew “tie sackcloth on your loins.”
Hebrew ‘ophel, the hill in Jerusalem south of the Temple. “Watchtower” is Hebrew bachan.
The Hebrew of this verse is hard, and the meaning is uncertain.

verses.text:
Shame on you, destroyer, when nobody has destroyed you.
Shame on you, traitor, when nobody has betrayed you.
Once you are done wrecking things, you will be wrecked.
Once you tire of treachery, others will turn on you.{a}

At the noise of your thunder the peoples run.
When you rise up, nations scatter.

Your loot is gathered up like a swarm of young locusts.
People rush on it like locusts jumping.

Yahweh is lifted high, for he lives on high.
He has filled Zion with justice and right living.

Listen, their heroes are shouting in the open.
Envoys sent to make peace are sobbing bitterly.{d}

The highways are empty.
No travelers walk them.
The treaty is broken.
The witnesses are scorned.
Nobody cares about human life.{e}

The land is mourning and wasting away.
Lebanon is ashamed and decays.
Sharon has become a dry plain,
and Bashan and Carmel have lost their leaves.{f}

“Now I will stand up,” says Yahweh.
“Now I will be lifted high.
Now I will be raised up.

You become pregnant with straw
and give birth to stubble.
Your own breath is a fire that will eat you up.

Peoples will be burned to lime,
like cut thorns thrown into a fire.

You in distant lands, hear what I have done.
You nearby, find out how strong I am.”

The sinners in Zion are terrified.
Shaking grips the godless.
“Which of us can live with a fire that eats everything?
Which of us can live with flames that never die?”

Whoever lives honestly and speaks truthfully,
who refuses money taken by force,
who waves a bribe away instead of grabbing it,
who covers his ears against plans to kill
and shuts his eyes against looking at evil,

that person will live on the heights.
His fortress will be a rocky stronghold.
His food will be provided,
and his water will never run out.

Your eyes will take in the king in his splendor.
They will look across a wide country.

You will never again see those fierce people,
a people whose speech is too strange to follow,
whose mocking language makes no sense to you.

Look at Zion, the city where we hold our feasts!
Your eyes will see Jerusalem,
a quiet settlement, a tent that will never be moved,
whose stakes will never be pulled out
and whose ropes will never snap.

There Yahweh will be our glorious God,
in a place of wide rivers and streams,
where no boats with oars will go
and no mighty ships will sail.

Yahweh is our judge.
Yahweh gives us our laws.
Yahweh is our king.
He will save us.{h}

Your ropes hang loose.
They cannot keep the mast in place
or hold the sail open.
Then a huge amount of loot will be divided,
and even the lame will carry off a share.

No resident will complain of being ill,
and the people there will be forgiven for their guilt.

notes.text: Some ancient copies read a little differently.
The Hebrew word for “kindness” can also be “favor.”
Or “Respect for Yahweh is Zion’s treasure.”
The Hebrew word for “brave men” (‘er’ellam) is uncertain. It may mean “Ariel” or “heroes.”
The Great Isaiah Scroll says “cities” for “witnesses.” “Witnesses” is Hebrew ‘arim, and “cities” would be ‘arim with different vowels.
Lebanon means “white.” Sharon was the coastal plain. Bashan was the highland east of the Sea of Galilee. Carmel was the wooded ridge by the coast.
Or “the one who counted the tribute.” These are Assyrian officers.
“Lawgiver” is Hebrew mechoqeq.

subheads.10: Who Can Live with the Fire?

verses.text:
Step up, you nations, and hear this!
Give your attention, you peoples!
Let the earth listen, with all that fills it,
the world and everything it produces.

Yahweh is angry at every nation
and furious at all their armies.
He has marked them for complete destruction
and handed them over for slaughter.{a}

Their dead will be thrown out,
their rotting bodies will stink,
and the mountains will run with their blood.

All the stars of the sky will rot away,
and the sky will roll up like a scroll.
All the stars will droop,
like leaves dropping from a vine,
like figs falling from a fig tree.{b}

Yahweh has a sword, and it is covered with blood.
It is smeared with fat,
the blood of lambs and goats,
and the kidney fat of rams.
Yahweh is holding a sacrifice in Bozrah,
and a great slaughter in Edom.{d}

Wild oxen will go down with them,
and young bulls with the strong bulls.
The land will be drenched in blood,
and the dust will turn greasy with fat.

This is Yahweh’s day of revenge,
the year when Zion’s case is settled.

Edom’s streams will turn to tar,
and her dust to burning sulfur.
Her land will become blazing tar.

It will burn night and day and never go out.
Its smoke will rise forever.
It will lie in ruins through all ages.
Nobody will ever cross it again.{e}

Owls and hedgehogs will take it over.
Great owls and ravens will nest there.
God will stretch over it a measuring line that makes it a wasteland,
and a plumb weight that leaves it empty.{f}

No nobles will be left to call a king,
and all her princes will be nothing.

Thorns will grow in her palaces,
and nettles and thistles in her forts.
She will be a lair for jackals
and a home for ostriches.

Desert cats will meet hyenas there,
and wild goats will call to each other.
The night creature will settle there
and find a place to rest.{g}

The owl will build a nest there and drop her eggs.
She will hatch them and shelter the chicks under her wings.
The vultures will gather there too,
each with its mate.{h}

Search the book of Yahweh and read it.
Not one of these will be missing.
None will lack its mate.
His own mouth gave the order,
and his Spirit brought them together.{i}

He drew lots for them,
and his hand measured out the land for them.
They will own it forever,
and they will live in it age after age.

notes.text: Hebrew herem, “set apart for destruction.” It means something given over completely to God.
The Great Isaiah Scroll and the Septuagint add “and the valleys will be split open.” Compare Revelation 6:13-14.
Edom means “red.” It was the land south of the Dead Sea, home of the descendants of Esau.
Bozrah, “sheepfold,” was a main city of Edom.
Compare Revelation 14:11 and 19:3.
Hebrew tohu and bohu, the words for “chaos” and “emptiness” used in Genesis 1:2. The identity of several birds in verses 11-15 is uncertain.
Hebrew lilith, a “night creature” (or night demon). Wild goat is se’ir.
The identity of these birds is uncertain.
Or “his mouth commanded” is read as “my mouth.” The Great Isaiah Scroll has small differences.

subheads.1: Judgment on the Nations and Edom

verses.text:
The wilderness and dry land will be glad.
The desert will cheer and burst into bloom like a crocus.{a}

It will bloom in great masses
and cheer with joyful song.
The glory of Lebanon will be handed to it,
with the splendor of Carmel and Sharon.
People will see Yahweh’s glory,
the splendor of our God.

Give strength to tired hands,
and steady the shaking knees.{b}

Tell the frightened,
“Be strong. Do not fear!
Look, your God is coming to pay back evil.
God will come with justice,
and he will save you.”

Then the eyes of the blind will open,
and the ears of the deaf will be unplugged.

Then the lame will jump like a deer,
and the tongue of the mute will sing.
Water will gush out in the wilderness,
and streams will flow in the desert.{c}

Burning sand will become a pond,
and thirsty ground will have bubbling springs.
In the lairs where jackals once lay,
grass will grow with reeds and rushes.{d}

A road will run through it, a highway,
and it will be called the Holy Road.
No unclean person will walk on it.
It will belong to those who walk the road,
and foolish people will not wander onto it.{e}

No lion will be there.
No fierce animal will climb onto it.
None of them will be found there.
Only the people Yahweh bought back will walk on it.

Those Yahweh has bought back will return.
They will enter Zion singing,
with joy that never ends crowning their heads.
Gladness and joy will catch up with them,
and sorrow and sighing will run away.{f}

notes.text: Or “autumn crocus” or “rose.” The Hebrew word is uncertain.
Compare Hebrews 12:12.
Compare Matthew 11:5 and Luke 7:22.
The Hebrew of the second half of this verse is hard to read.
Hebrew derekh haqqodesh. The Hebrew of the last two lines is uncertain.
The last verse is nearly the same as 51:11.

verses.text: In King Hezekiah’s fourteenth year, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked every walled city in Judah and captured them.{a}

The Assyrian king sent his chief officer, called the Rabshakeh, from Lachish to King Hezekiah in Jerusalem, with a large army. The officer stopped at the water channel from the upper pool, beside the road to the Washer’s Field.{b}
Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who ran the palace, went out to meet him. Shebna the secretary and Joah son of Asaph, the record keeper, went with him.{c}
The Rabshakeh told them, “Give Hezekiah this message from the great king, the king of Assyria: What is this confidence you are leaning on?
You say you have a plan and the strength to fight, but those are only empty words. Who are you counting on, that you dared to rebel against me?{d}
Look, you are counting on Egypt, a snapped reed. If a man leans on it, it jabs into his hand and pierces it. Pharaoh king of Egypt does the same to everyone who trusts him.

Or maybe you will tell me, ‘We trust in Yahweh our God.’ But is he not the one whose hilltop shrines and altars Hezekiah tore down? Did Hezekiah not tell Judah and Jerusalem, ‘You must worship at this one altar’?
Come now, strike a bargain with my master the king of Assyria. I will give you two thousand horses if you can supply enough riders to sit on them.
You could not beat back even one of the lowest officers in my master’s army. Yet you trust Egypt for chariots and riders.
And do you think I came up against this land to wreck it without Yahweh? Yahweh himself told me, ‘March on this land and wipe it out.’”
Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to the chief officer, “Please talk to us in Aramaic. We understand it. Do not speak in the language of Judah, because the people on the wall can hear you.”{e}

The Rabshakeh answered, “Did my master send me to say these things only to your master and you? Did he not send me to the men sitting on the wall, who will eat their own dung and drink their own urine with you?”
Then the officer stood and shouted in the language of Judah, “Listen to what the great king, the king of Assyria, says!
This is what the king says: Do not let Hezekiah fool you. He cannot save you.
Do not let Hezekiah talk you into trusting Yahweh when he says, ‘Yahweh will surely save us. The king of Assyria will not take this city.’

Do not listen to Hezekiah. Here is the Assyrian king’s offer: ‘Come to terms with me and surrender. Then every one of you will have grapes from his own vine, figs from his own tree, and water from his own well,{f}
until I come and take you to a land like your own, a land of grain and new wine, of bread and vineyards.
Make sure Hezekiah does not mislead you with his claim, “Yahweh will rescue us.” Has any god of any nation rescued his land from the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Did they save Samaria from me?{g}
Which of the gods of all these lands saved their land from me? So how can Yahweh save Jerusalem from me?’”
The people stayed silent and answered not a word, because the king had commanded, “Do not reply to him.”

Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who ran the palace, together with Shebna the secretary and Joah son of Asaph, the record keeper, came to Hezekiah with their clothes ripped open. They reported to him what the chief officer had said.

notes.text: Hezekiah’s fourteenth year was about 701 BC. Sennacherib means “Sin (the moon god) has replaced the brothers.” Assyria was the great power of northern Mesopotamia. Compare 2 Kings 18:13-19:37.

“Rabshakeh” is an Assyrian title meaning “chief officer” or “chief cupbearer.” Lachish was a strong city of Judah, southwest of Jerusalem. The Washer’s Field can also be “Fuller’s Field.” Compare 7:3.
Eliakim means “God raises up.” Hilkiah means “my portion is Yahweh.” Shebna may be short for Shebaniah. Joah means “Yahweh is brother.” Asaph means “he gathers.”
Or “mere words of the lips.”
Aramaic was the language used between nations then. “The language of Judah” is Hebrew.
Hebrew “make a blessing with me,” which means to make a peace deal.
Hamath and Arpad were Syrian cities. Sepharvaim was a city taken by Assyria (compare 2 Kings 17:24). Samaria was the capital of the northern kingdom of Israel.

verses.text: Hezekiah heard the report and ripped his robe. He wrapped himself in sackcloth and entered Yahweh’s house.
He also sent Eliakim the palace manager, Shebna the secretary, and the older priests, all dressed in sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
They said to him, “Hezekiah says: Today is a day of pain, correction, and shame. It is like a woman ready to give birth who has no strength left to push.{a}

Perhaps Yahweh your God heard everything the Rabshakeh said. His boss, the Assyrian king, sent him to curse the living God. Perhaps Yahweh your God will answer those words. Please pray for those of us who are still left.”{b}
When King Hezekiah’s officials came to Isaiah,
Isaiah told them, “Say this to your master: Yahweh says, ‘Do not be afraid because of the words you heard, the insults the Assyrian king’s young men threw at me.{c}
Hear me: a spirit will be sent into him by my doing. He will receive some news and go back to his own land. There I will have him fall by the sword.’”
The Rabshakeh went back. He found the Assyrian king fighting at Libnah, because he had learned the king had moved on from Lachish.{d}
Then word reached the king about Tirhakah, the king of Cush: “He has marched out to attack you.” When Sennacherib got this news, he sent messengers to Hezekiah with a letter saying:{e}
“Give Hezekiah king of Judah this message: ‘Do not let your God, whom you trust, fool you with the promise that Jerusalem will never fall to the king of Assyria.
You know what the Assyrian kings have done to every land, wiping them off the map. Why would you be the exception?
Those peoples’ gods did not save them. My forefathers destroyed Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the Edenites living at Telassar.{f}
Where is Hamath’s king, or Arpad’s? Where are the rulers of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?’”{g}
From the messengers’ hands Hezekiah took the letter and read it. Then he climbed to Yahweh’s house and unrolled it before Yahweh.
Hezekiah prayed to Yahweh:
“Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel, you sit on your throne above the winged guardians. You alone are God of every kingdom on earth. You made heaven and earth.{h}
Bend down your ear, Yahweh, and listen. Open your eyes, Yahweh, and look. Listen to every word Sennacherib sent to insult the living God.
It is a fact, Yahweh, that the Assyrian kings have ruined all these peoples and their lands.{i}
They tossed those peoples’ gods into flames. Those were never gods, just wood and stone carved by hands, so Assyria could smash them.
Now, Yahweh our God, rescue us from his hand. Then every kingdom on earth will realize you are the only Yahweh.”{j}
Isaiah son of Amoz sent Hezekiah a reply: “Yahweh, the God of Israel, says: ‘You asked me for help against Sennacherib king of Assyria.

here is Yahweh’s word against him:
“Zion, the young woman,
scorns you and laughs at you.
Jerusalem, her daughter,
wags her head as you run away.

Whom did you mock and insult?
Against whom did you shout
and look up with such pride?
Against the Holy One of Israel!

You used your servants to mock the Lord.
You boasted, ‘With my crowd of chariots
I have climbed the highest mountains,
the far ends of Lebanon.
I felled its tallest cedars
and its finest cypresses.
I went to its farthest peak,
its thickest woods.{k}

Have you never been told
that I planned this ages ago?
In days long past I shaped it.
Now I have brought it about,
and you are the one who turns fortified cities
into heaps of stones.

Their people had little strength.
They were terrified and ashamed.
They were like grass in the field, like tender green plants,
like grass on the roof,
scorched before it grows tall.{m}

But I know where you sit,
when you go out and when you come home,
and how you rave against me.

Since you rave against me,
and your pride has come to my ears,
I will hook your nose
and put a bit between your lips.
I will haul you back
by the same road you took.”{n}

As proof, this is what will happen. This year you will live on whatever sprouts by itself. In year two you will live on what comes up from that. In year three you will sow and reap, and you will plant vineyards and eat their grapes.
The survivors of Judah’s family will put roots down again below and bear fruit above.
A few will come out of Jerusalem, and survivors from Mount Zion. The passion of Yahweh of Armies will do this.{o}
So here is what Yahweh says about the king of Assyria: He will not set foot in this city. He will not fire an arrow into it. He will not bring a shield up to it or pile up an assault ramp against it.
He will return by the road he used to arrive. He will not set foot in this city, says Yahweh.
I will defend this city and save it, for my own sake and for the sake of my servant David.’”
That night Yahweh’s angel went out and struck down 185,000 men in the Assyrian camp. At dawn the survivors rose and saw dead bodies lying all over the ground.{p}
So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and left. He returned to Nineveh and stayed there.{q}

Once, while he was bowing down in the temple of his god Nisroch, his own sons Adrammelech and Sharezer cut him down with swords. Then they escaped into the land of Ararat, and another son, Esarhaddon, took the throne.{r}

notes.text: Hebrew “children have come to birth but there is no strength to bring them out.”
The Rabshakeh was the Assyrian chief officer (see 36:2).
Hebrew “young men,” meaning the king’s servants.
Libnah, “white,” was a city of Judah near Lachish. Lachish was the strong city southwest of Jerusalem.
Tirhakah was a Cushite (Nubian) ruler of Egypt. His name is Egyptian Taharqa. Cush was the land south of Egypt. Sennacherib means “Sin (the moon god) has replaced the brothers.”
Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and Telassar were cities in the Assyrian lands of Mesopotamia and Syria. Eden here means Beth-eden, an Aramean kingdom.
Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah were cities and lands in Syria and Mesopotamia that Assyria took.
Hebrew “above the cherubim.” Cherubim are winged guardians that stood over the lid of the Ark.
Some copies say “all the lands” here.
Some ancient copies say “you alone, Yahweh, are God.”
The Hebrew says “the height of Lebanon.” The “far ends” is the farthest part.
Hebrew Matsor, a name for Egypt. Compare 2 Kings 19:24.
Hebrew “grass before it stands up.” The meaning is clear, but the form of the word is unusual.
The picture comes from how Assyria led captives and animals with hooks and rings.
In some ancient copies verse 32 reads “the passion of Yahweh” without “of Armies.”
The number 185,000 is as written in 2 Kings 19:35.
Nineveh was the capital of Assyria, on the Tigris River.

Nisroch is the name of an Assyrian god, and the form of the name is uncertain. Adrammelech means “Adrammelech is king” (?). Sharezer means “protect the king” (?). Ararat is the land of Urartu, in the mountains of eastern Turkey. Esarhaddon ruled Assyria from 681 to 669 BC.

subheads.36: The Assyrian Army Is Struck Down

verses.text: About then Hezekiah became so sick that he was dying. Isaiah son of Amoz, the prophet, went to him and said, “Yahweh says: Get your house ready, because you will die. You will not get better.”{a}
Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to Yahweh.
He said, “Yahweh, please remember how I have lived before you, loyal and with all my heart. I have done what you consider good.” Then Hezekiah cried and cried.
Yahweh’s word came to Isaiah:
“Go to Hezekiah and tell him, ‘Yahweh, the God of your forefather David, says: Your prayer has reached me, and I have watched your tears fall. See, I am giving you fifteen more years.
I will also rescue you and this city from the Assyrian king, and I will defend this city.{b}
Here is the sign from Yahweh that he will do what he promised:
Look, I will make the shadow on the steps of Ahaz go back ten steps, the same steps it already went down in the sun.’” And the sunlight went back ten steps on the stairs where it had gone down.{c}
This is a poem by Hezekiah king of Judah after he was sick and got well:{d}

I said, “I will never see Yah,
never see Yah in the land of the living.
I will not look at any other human being again
among those who live in this world.”{f}

My home is pulled up and carried off,
like a shepherd’s tent.
I have rolled up my life like a weaver rolls up cloth.
He cuts me from the loom.
Between morning and night you finish me off.{g}

I peep like a swift or crane.
I coo sadly like a dove.
My eyes are weak from staring at the sky.
Lord, I am being crushed. Step in for me!{i}

What can I say? He spoke to me,
and he is the one who did it.
I will walk carefully all my years
because of the bitterness I feel.{j}

See, my bitter pain
turned out to be for my good.
You loved me, and so you pulled my soul
back from the pit of ruin.
You flung every one of my sins behind you.{l}

The grave cannot give you thanks.
Death cannot sing your praise.
Those who sink into the pit
cannot hope for your loyalty.

Only the living can thank you,
only the living, as I do today.
Fathers tell their children
about your faithfulness.

Yahweh is ready to rescue me.
We will strum my songs on stringed instruments
every day of our lives
in the house of Yahweh.{m}
Isaiah had said, “Make a paste from a cake of figs and spread it on the boil, so he will get well.”{n}
Hezekiah had asked, “What is the sign that I will go up to Yahweh’s house?”

notes.text: Hezekiah’s illness may have been in about 703 BC. Compare 2 Kings 20:1-11 and 2 Chronicles 32:24.
This verse puts the promise to free the city before the Assyrian crisis in chapters 36-37. The events in chapters 36-39 are not in time order.
The “steps” may have been stairs used as a sundial. A step could also mean a “degree.” Ahaz was Hezekiah’s father.
Verses 9-20 are not in 2 Kings 20. The Hebrew of this poem is hard, and the meaning of some lines is uncertain.
Or “in the quiet of my days.” Hebrew Sheol, the place of the dead.
Yah is a short form of Yahweh. Some read “I will not see Yah in the land of the living” as “I will not see his face in the land of the living.”
Hebrew “between day and night.” It means “quickly,” or “all at once.”
Or “I made myself quiet until morning.” The Hebrew is uncertain.
Or “I chirp like a swift or a crane.” The birds are uncertain. “Stand up for me” means be my guarantor.
The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain.
The Hebrew of this verse is very hard to read.
Or “you held my soul from the pit.” Throwing sins “behind the back” means to forgive them.
The “stringed instruments” are for singing. Hebrew “my songs.”
Verses 21-22 are out of order in the Hebrew text. Compare 2 Kings 20:7-8.

verses.text: Around that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan, who ruled Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah. He had learned that Hezekiah had been ill and was well again.{a}

Hezekiah was delighted. He took the visitors through his storehouse of valuables, showing them the silver, the gold, the spices, the fine oil, his whole armory, and everything in his treasuries. Nothing in his palace or in all his realm was kept from them.{b}
Then the prophet Isaiah went to King Hezekiah and questioned him: “What did these men say? Where did they come from?” Hezekiah replied, “From a distant land. They traveled here from Babylon.”
Isaiah asked, “What did they look at in your palace?” Hezekiah said, “They looked at everything in my palace. I did not hide even one treasure from them.”
Isaiah told Hezekiah, “Hear what Yahweh of Armies says:
Days are coming when all that is in your palace, and all that your forefathers have saved to this day, will be hauled off to Babylon. Nothing will remain, says Yahweh.
Some of your own descendants, your own sons, will be taken away. They will become palace officials for the king of Babylon.”{c}
Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “The word of Yahweh that you have spoken is good.” For he thought, “At least there will be peace and safety while I am alive.”{d}

notes.text: Merodach-baladan (Babylonian Marduk-apla-iddina) means “the god Marduk has given an heir.” Babylon is a city on the Euphrates River. He ruled Babylon for periods between 721 and 703 BC.
The Hebrew for “treasure house” can also be “house of his treasures.” “Fine oil” is olive oil.
Hebrew saris, “eunuch,” a palace official. It can mean a man who was made a eunuch.
Hebrew “peace and truth.”

verses.text:
“Comfort my people. Comfort them,”
says your God.{a}

“Speak warmly to Jerusalem.
Tell her that her time of hard service is over,
that her guilt has been paid,
and that she has received from Yahweh’s hand
twice what her sins deserved.”{b}

A voice cries out:
“Clear the road for Yahweh in the desert.
Level a highway for our God
across the wasteland.{c}

Every valley is to be filled in,
and every mountain and hill is to be leveled.
The bumpy ground will be smoothed,
and the rocky ground will be made flat.{d}

A voice says, “Call out!”
Another asks, “What should I call out?”
“Human beings are like grass,
and all their loyalty is like wildflowers in the field.{f}

The grass dries up and the flowers fade,
but our God’s word stands firm forever.”{h}

Go up a high mountain,
Zion, bringer of good news.
Raise your voice and shout,
Jerusalem, bringer of good news.
Shout it, and have no fear.
Announce to Judah’s towns,
“Your God is here!”{i}

See, the Lord Yahweh arrives with power,
and his arm rules for him.
See, he carries his reward,
and his payment goes ahead of him.{j}

Like a shepherd he looks after his flock.
He gathers the lambs in his arms
and carries them next to his heart.
He leads the nursing mothers with gentleness.

Who has scooped up the seas in a cupped hand,
or measured the sky with a hand span?
Who has packed the earth’s dust in a basket,
or weighed the mountains on scales
and the hills on a balance?{k}

Who has taken the measure of Yahweh’s Spirit,
or taught him as his adviser?{l}

Whom did he ask for advice to gain understanding?
Who taught him the path of justice,
or gave him knowledge,
or showed him the way to insight?

Lebanon’s trees would not be enough for the fire,
and its animals would not be enough for an offering.

All the nations are nothing in front of him.
To him they are less than nothing, empty and worthless.{n}

So whom will you liken to God?
What image can you put next to him?

Someone too poor for an expensive gift
chooses a wood that will not decay.
He searches for a skilled carver
to set up an idol that will not wobble.{p}

Do you not know? Have you not heard?
Were you not told from the beginning?
Have you not grasped how the earth was founded?

He is seated above the circle of the earth,
and its people look like locusts.
He spreads out the sky like a sheer cloth
and stretches it over us like a tent for living in.{q}

He brings princes to nothing
and makes the earth’s judges worthless.{r}

They have barely been planted, barely sown,
barely sent their roots into the ground,
and he puffs on them, and they shrivel,
and a whirlwind lifts them away like chaff.

“So who will you compare me to?
Who is my equal?” says the Holy One.

Lift up your eyes and look.
Who created all of these?
He marches out their army by number
and calls each by name.
Because his strength is so vast and his power so great,
not one of them is absent.{s}

Jacob, why do you grumble?
Israel, why do you claim,
“Yahweh does not see my way,
and my God ignores my rights”?

Do you not know? Have you not heard?
Yahweh is the everlasting God,
the Creator of the ends of the earth.
He does not get tired or worn out.
No one can measure his understanding.

He gives strength to the tired
and adds power to those with none.{t}

Even young people get tired and worn out,
and young men stumble and fall.

But those who wait for Yahweh will have their strength renewed.
They will lift off on wings like eagles.
They will run and not tire.
They will walk and not grow weary.{u}

notes.text: Chapters 40-66 speak to the people of Judah during and after the exile in Babylon (about 586-539 BC). “Your God” is Hebrew ‘eloheykem.
Hebrew “twice.” It may mean “the full amount.”
Matthew 3:3, Mark 1:3, Luke 3:4-6, and John 1:23 apply verses 3-5 to John the Baptist. They follow the Septuagint, which reads “a voice cries out in the desert.”
Hebrew “the bumpy will become level (ground) and the rough places a plain.”
The Septuagint says “and all flesh will see the saving power of God.”
Hebrew hesed (“loyal love”). The Septuagint says “all its glory is like a flower of grass.”
The Great Isaiah Scroll does not have the last line of verse 7. 1 Peter 1:24-25 quotes verses 6-8.
Some ancient copies read a little differently.
Or “Zion, bringer of good news” can also be “O messenger of good news to Zion.”
Or “his reward is for him.”
Hebrew shaal (hollow of his hand), zeret (“span”), shalish (“a measure,” about a third). “Width of his hand” is the span, about 9 inches (23 centimeters).
Paul quotes verses 13-14 in Romans 11:34 and 1 Corinthians 2:16 from the Septuagint.
Or “coastlands.”
Some ancient copies read a little differently.
The Hebrew of verses 19-20 is hard.
Hebrew terumah, “offering.”
Or “a tent to live in” is Hebrew “a tent to dwell.”
The Hebrew word for “worthless” is tohu, as in Genesis 1:2 (“empty”).
The Hebrew says “not one is missing.”
Some ancient copies add “and to those with no strength he gives more power.”
Hebrew qavah, “to wait” or “to hope.” Some ancient copies say “they will grow new wings.”

verses.text:
“Island peoples, be silent in front of me.
Nations, gather your strength.
Step forward and speak.
Let us meet together for the trial.{a}

Who woke up a man in the east,
whom victory meets at every step?
He hands nations over to that man
and makes him walk over kings.
His sword turns them into dust,
and his bow turns them into blowing straw.{b}

He chases them and moves on safely,
on a road his feet have never walked.{c}

Who did this and made it happen,
calling the generations from the very start?
I, Yahweh, was there first,
and I will be there with the last. I am the one.”{d}

Each one helps his neighbor,
and tells his brother, “Be brave!”

The carpenter pats the goldsmith on the back.
The man who smooths with a mallet praises the one who hits the anvil.
Of the soldering he says, “Nice work.”
Then he nails the idol in place so it cannot topple.

I fetched you from the farthest ends of the earth
and summoned you from its remotest corners.
I said, “You serve me.
I picked you, and I have not tossed you aside.”

Never fear, since I am beside you.
Never look around in panic, since I am your God.
My strength will be yours, and my help will come.
My victorious right hand will hold you steady.{g}

See, everyone who rages at you
will be shamed and embarrassed.
Those who fight you
will be as nothing and will die out.{h}

You will hunt for your attackers
and not find them.
The men who make war on you
will be nothing, less than nothing.

I am Yahweh your God.
I hold your right hand.
I tell you, “Do not fear.
I will help you.”

Never fear, tiny worm Jacob,
you handful of Israel.
I will be your help, says Yahweh.
The one who buys you back is the Holy One of Israel.{i}

Now I have turned you into a threshing sledge,
new and sharp, with many teeth.
You will crush the mountains and grind them fine,
and you will turn the hills into chaff.{j}

You will toss them up, and the wind will blow them away,
and a gale will scatter them.
Then you will celebrate Yahweh
and boast about Israel’s Holy One.

Poor and needy people hunt for water, and there is none.
Their tongues stick to the roofs of their mouths from thirst.
I, Yahweh, will give them an answer.
I, Israel’s God, will never walk away from them.

I will make rivers flow on bald hills
and springs bubble up in valleys.
The wilderness will become a lake,
and parched ground will turn to springs.

I will plant cedars in the wasteland,
with acacia, myrtle, and olive trees.
I will set juniper in the desert,
with plane trees and pines next to it,{k}

so that people will see and know,
think about it and understand together,
that Yahweh’s hand did this,
and the Holy One of Israel made it.

“Present your case,” says Yahweh.
“Bring your best arguments,” says Jacob’s King.

Bring your idols here to tell us
what is going to happen.
Tell us how things began,
so we can reflect on them
and find out how they turned out.
Or let us hear what is coming.{l}

Tell us what is coming in the future,
so we will know you are gods.
Do something, good or bad,
so we will be shocked and all see it.{m}

I woke a man in the north, and he has arrived,
one from where the sun rises, who will call on my name.
He will march over rulers like wet plaster,
the way a potter stomps on clay.{o}

Who announced this at the start, so we could know,
or long ago, so we could say, ‘He is right’?
None of you declared it, and none of you announced it.
No one heard you say a word.

I was first to tell Zion, ‘Look, here they come!’
I give Jerusalem a messenger with good news.{p}

I look, but no one is there.
Among these idols there is no adviser
who can answer when I ask.

notes.text: “Island peoples” is Hebrew ‘iyyim, “coastlands” or “islands,” meaning far-off lands across the sea.
The “man in the east” is probably Cyrus of Persia. Compare 44:28 and 45:1. Hebrew “whom righteousness calls to its foot.”
Hebrew “on a path with his feet he does not go.”
Compare Revelation 1:17 and 22:13.
Hebrew “they drew near and came” can also be “they came together.”
Abraham means “father of many.” Yahweh calls him “my friend” (see 2 Chronicles 20:7 and James 2:23).
Or “my right hand of victory.”
Hebrew “the men of your quarrel.”
Hebrew go’el, “Redeemer,” a family member who buys back one who is in trouble. “Few people” is Hebrew “men of Israel.”
Hebrew morag, a threshing sledge with sharp stones or iron teeth.
Acacia is Hebrew shittah. The names of several of these trees are uncertain.
Or “the former things, what were they?”
Or “so we may look at each other in fear.”
The Septuagint says “you are from nothing, and your work is from the earth.”
The man “from the north” and “from the east” is Cyrus. Some ancient copies read a little differently.
The Hebrew of this verse is hard. Some read “I first said to Zion, ‘Look, look at them.’”
Hebrew tohu, “emptiness.”

subheads.21: The Idols Have Nothing to Say

verses.text:
“Here is my servant, the one I hold up,
my chosen one, who pleases me deeply.
I have put my Spirit on him.
He will bring justice to the nations.{a}

He will not yell or speak loudly.
His voice will not carry down the street.

This is what God, Yahweh, says.
He made the heavens and stretched them out.
He pounded the earth flat, with all that comes from it.
He supplies breath for its people
and life for those who walk on it.{d}

“I am Yahweh. I called you to act with justice.
I will grab your hand and keep you safe.
I will make you a pledge to the people,
a light for the nations,{e}

to open eyes that cannot see,
to lead prisoners out of the dungeon,
and to bring out of the jail
those who sit in the dark.

I am Yahweh. That is my name.
I will not hand my glory to anyone else,
or my praise to carved statues.

See, the earlier events have taken place,
and I now declare new ones.
I tell you about them
before they spring up.”

Sing a new song to Yahweh,
his praise from the far corners of the earth.
Sing, you who sail the sea and all that lives in it,
you islands and everyone on them.{f}

Let the desert and its towns lift their voices,
and the camps where the Kedar tribe lives.
Let the people of Sela sing for joy.
Let them shout from mountain peaks.{g}

Let them give glory to Yahweh
and spread his praise across the islands.

Yahweh marches out like a fighter.
Like a soldier, he works up his passion.
He cries out and roars the war cry.
He proves stronger than his enemies.{h}

“I have been silent a long time.
I have kept quiet and held back.
Now I will cry out in pain, like a woman giving birth.
I will pant and gasp for air.

I will make mountains and hills bare
and dry up all the plants on them.
I will change rivers into dry islands
and dry out the pools.{i}

I will lead blind people
along roads they have never traveled.
I will steer them down paths unknown to them.
I will turn darkness ahead of them into light
and rough ground into level plains.
I will do all this,
and I will not leave them behind.”

Those who trust in carved statues will be turned back
and covered with shame.
They tell metal idols,
“You are our gods.”

“Hear this, you deaf people!
Look, you blind people, and see!

Who is blind except my servant?
Who is deaf like the messenger I am sending?
Who is as blind as my partner,
as blind as Yahweh’s servant?{j}

You see much, but you take in nothing.
Your ears are wide open, but nothing registers.”{k}

Because Yahweh is just, he was pleased
to make his teaching great and glorious.{l}

Yet these are people who have been robbed and looted.
Every one of them is stuck in a hole
or hidden in a prison.
They have become spoil, and no one rescues them.
They have become loot, and no one says, “Send them back!”{m}

Which of you will give an ear to this?
Who will listen closely from now on?

Who handed Jacob over to be plundered,
and Israel to robbers?
Was it not Yahweh, the one we sinned against?
They would not walk in his ways
or obey his teaching.{n}

So he poured his blazing anger on Israel,
and the violence of war.
It set Israel on fire all around, yet Israel did not realize it.
It scorched them, yet they did not take it to heart.{o}

notes.text: Matthew 12:18-21 quotes verses 1-4. Some see the servant as Israel, and others as one person.
Hebrew “in truth (or faithfulness) he will bring out justice.”
Hebrew ‘iyyim, “islands” or “coastlands.”
The Septuagint adds “Jacob, my servant, I will help him” at the start of verse 1. The Great Isaiah Scroll has a small difference in verse 5.
Or “a covenant for the people.” Hebrew berit ‘am, “agreement for a people.” Compare 49:6.
Hebrew “you who go down to the sea.” The Septuagint says “you who sail on the sea.”
Kedar means “dark.” It was a tribe of Arab nomads (Genesis 25:13). Sela means “rock,” a mountain stronghold in Edom.
Hebrew “he proves himself mighty against his enemies.”
Or “I will turn rivers into dry land.”
The word for “agreement” is Hebrew meshullam. It is uncertain. It may mean “the one at peace with me” or “the one I have paid.”
Some ancient copies read “you see many things, but he does not notice.”
Or “his teaching” (torah).
Hebrew “plunder and no one says, ‘Give back!’”
Or “instruction” (Hebrew torah).
Some ancient copies read a little differently.

verses.text:
But now Yahweh says this,
the one who made you, Jacob,
and who formed you, Israel:
“Fear nothing, for I have paid to bring you back.
I have called you by your name. You are mine.

When you pass through the waters, I will go with you.
When you cross rivers, they will not drown you.
When you walk into fire, you will not be burned,
and the blaze will not singe you.

I am Yahweh your God,
the Holy One of Israel, who saves you.
I gave Egypt to pay for your freedom,
and Cush and Seba in your place.{a}

You are valuable to me.
I honor you, and I love you.
So I trade other people for you,
and entire nations for your life.

Fear nothing, for I am at your side.
I will bring your offspring from the sunrise,
and I will round you up from the sunset.

I will order the north, ‘Hand them over!’
and the south, ‘Do not keep them!’
Bring my sons from distant places
and my daughters from the earth’s far edges,

everyone who is called by my name,
whom I made for my glory,
whom I shaped, yes, whom I formed.’”

Call out the blind who have eyes,
and the deaf who have ears.

Let all the nations assemble
and the peoples come together.
Which of their gods could have said this
or told us about earlier days?

“You are my witnesses,” says Yahweh,
“the servant I selected,
so that you will know me, put your faith in me,
and understand that I am the one.
No god was made before me,
and no god will follow me.{b}

I, I am Yahweh,
and there is no savior except me.

I was the one who spoke, who saved, and who made it known,
when no strange god was among you.
You are my witnesses,” says Yahweh. “I am God.

Yahweh, your Redeemer,
the Holy One of Israel, says this:
“I have dispatched a force against Babylon for you.
I will make them all run,
the Chaldeans too, who cheer in their ships.{d}

I am Yahweh, your Holy One,
the Creator of Israel, your King.”

This is what Yahweh says,
who makes a road through the sea
and a path through rushing water,

who calls out chariots and horses,
army and warriors together.
They lie down and cannot get up.
They are put out like the flame of a wick:

“Do not dwell on the past.
Do not think about old events.

Look, I am doing a new thing.
It is already coming up. Can you not see it?
I will lay a road through the wilderness
and rivers across the desert.{e}

Wild animals will honor me,
jackals and ostriches too,
because I give water in the wilderness
and rivers in the desert,
to give a drink to my chosen people,

the people I shaped for myself
so they would tell of my praise.

Yet you did not call on me, Jacob.
You got sick of me, Israel.

You brought me no sheep for the fire.
You gave me no honor with your sacrifices.
I never forced you to work with grain offerings,
or tired you out with incense.{f}

You did not buy fragrant cane for me with your silver.
You did not fill me up with the fat of your sacrifices.
Instead you made me carry your sins.
You exhausted me with your wrongs.{g}

Remind me. Let us argue the case together.
Speak up so that you can be proved right.

Your earliest ancestor sinned,
and your spokesmen turned against me.{i}

notes.text: Seba was a land in the upper Nile region, near Cush. Cush was south of Egypt.
Some ancient copies read a little differently.
Or “no one can rescue from my hand.”
The Chaldeans were the people of southern Babylonia. The Hebrew of the last line is uncertain. It may be “the Chaldeans, in the ships they were so proud of.”
Compare Revelation 21:5.
Hebrew minhah, “grain offering.”
“Sweet cane” is Hebrew qaneh, a fragrant reed used in worship (Exodus 30:23).
Hebrew “I will not remember your sins.”
The “first father” may be Adam, Abraham, or Jacob.
Or “I will put the leaders of the holy place under the ban (herem).” The word means set apart for destruction.

verses.text:
“But now listen, Jacob, my servant,
Israel, the one I picked.

This is what Yahweh says, who made you
and shaped you in the womb and helps you:
Do not be afraid, Jacob, my servant,
Jeshurun, the one I picked.{a}

I will soak the thirsty soil
and send streams across dry ground.
My Spirit will fall on your children,
and my blessing will rest on your descendants.

They will shoot up like grass beside the water,
like poplar trees along streams.{b}

One will say, ‘I belong to Yahweh.’
Another will take the name Jacob.
Another will write on his hand, ‘Yahweh’s,’
and take the name Israel for his own.”{c}

Who is like me? Let that one speak up,
explain it, and lay it out before me,
from the time I set up the ancient people.
Let them tell what is coming
and what will happen.{e}

Do not tremble or be afraid.
Did I not tell you about this ages ago?
You are my witnesses!
Does another God exist?
There is no other Rock. I know of none.”{f}

People who carve idols are all nothing,
and the things they treasure help no one.
Those who speak for the idols see nothing and know nothing,
so they will be ashamed.{g}

Who would shape a god or pour a metal statue
that cannot help at all?

See, all who work with him will be ashamed.
The workmen are only human.
Let them all gather and stand up together.
They will be scared and shamed together.

The blacksmith takes a tool
and labors over the hot coals.
He pounds the iron with hammers
and works it with his strong arm.
But he gets hungry and his strength gives out.
He skips his water and grows faint.

The carpenter pulls out a measuring cord
and draws an outline with a marker.
He carves it with chisels
and outlines it with a compass.
He shapes it like a man,
with the good looks of a human body,
to sit inside a shrine.{h}

He cuts down cedars,
or picks a cypress or an oak
and lets it get sturdy among the other forest trees.
Or he plants a pine, and the rain feeds it.{i}

Later it becomes fuel for people.
Some of it he uses to keep warm.
He also kindles a fire and bakes his bread.
Yet from the same wood he makes a god and worships!
He carves an idol and bows low to it.

Half of the wood he burns in a fire.
Over its coals he roasts meat and eats until he is full.
He also warms his hands and says,
“Ah, that feels good. I can see the flames!”

From the rest he makes a god, his own idol.
He drops to his knees and worships it.
He prays to it and says,
“Rescue me! You are my god!”

Nobody stops to reflect.
Nobody has the knowledge or sense to say,
“I burned half of it in the fire.
I even baked my loaves on its coals.
I roasted meat on them and ate it.
So why should I turn the rest into something disgusting?
Why should I bow to a chunk of wood?”{k}

“Keep these things in mind, Jacob,
and you, Israel, because you are my servant.
I shaped you to serve me.
Israel, I will never forget you.{m}

I have swept away your rebellion like a thick cloud
and your sins like morning mist.
Come back to me, because I have bought you back.”

Sing for joy, heavens, for Yahweh has done this.
Shout, you deep places of the earth.
Burst into song, you mountains,
you forest and every tree in it.
For Yahweh has bought Jacob back,
and he shows his glory in Israel.{n}

This is what Yahweh says, the one who buys you back
and formed you in the womb:
“I am Yahweh, maker of everything.
By myself I stretched out the sky.
I spread out the earth. Who was with me?{o}

I make the signs of false prophets fail
and make fools of fortune-tellers.
I turn wise men back
and make their knowledge foolish.{p}

I make the word of my servant come true
and carry out the plans of my messengers.
I say of Jerusalem, ‘People will live there,’
and of the towns of Judah, ‘They will be rebuilt,
and I will repair their ruins.’{q}

I tell the deep waters, ‘Be dry.
I will dry up your rivers.’{r}

I tell Cyrus, ‘You are my shepherd.
You will carry out all my wishes.’
I tell Jerusalem, ‘You will be rebuilt,’
and I tell the Temple, ‘Your foundation will be laid.’”{s}

notes.text: Jeshurun means “upright one,” a poetic name for Israel (Deuteronomy 32:15).
Hebrew “poplars by flowing streams.” The Septuagint says “willows.”
Hebrew “write on his hand,” like a mark of ownership. Jacob is the family name for the people.
Compare Revelation 1:17 and 22:13.
Or “from the time I set up an ancient people.”
“Rock” is Hebrew tsur, a title for God.
Some ancient copies read a little differently.
The Hebrew words for the tools in verse 13 are uncertain.
Hebrew ‘oren, probably a kind of pine.
Some ancient copies read a little differently.
Hebrew to’evah, “something disgusting.”
Hebrew “ashes.” Compare Hosea 12:1.
Some ancient copies read “do not forget me” for “I will not forget you.”
Hebrew “he glorifies himself in Israel.”
The Great Isaiah Scroll reads “who was with me?” as “who was by me?” The Hebrew text can be read either way.
Hebrew baddim, “boasters” or “false prophets.”
Some ancient copies read a little differently.
Hebrew “the deep,” a sea or flood.
Cyrus (Hebrew Koresh) was king of Persia, who allowed Jews to go home in 538 BC. His name probably means “sun” or “young.” The Septuagint puts “who says to Cyrus” a little differently.

verses.text:
Here is what Yahweh says about Cyrus, his anointed one.
Yahweh took hold of his right hand
to bring nations under his power,
to take away the belts of kings,
and to open doors in front of him
so that no gates stay closed:{a}

“I will go in front of you
and flatten the hills.
I will break down bronze gates
and cut through iron bolts.{b}

I will give you treasures stored in the dark,
wealth hidden in secret places,
so that you will know I am Yahweh,
the God of Israel, who calls you by name.

For the sake of my servant Jacob,
and Israel, whom I picked,
I have called you by your name.
I have given you a title of honor, though you have not known me.{c}

I am Yahweh, and no one else is.
No God exists but me.
I will make you strong, though you have not known me,

so that people from sunrise to sunset will know
that no one else exists.
I am Yahweh, and there is no second.

“Sky above, drop down your dew.
Clouds, pour down justice.
Earth, open wide so rescue can sprout
and justice can grow with it.
I, Yahweh, have made it happen.”{e}

What sorrow for anyone who argues with his Maker,
one broken pot among the pots on the ground!
Will clay ask the potter, “What are you making?”
Will your work say, “He has no hands”?{f}

What sorrow for anyone who tells a father, “What have you brought into the world?”
or tells a mother, “What have you given birth to?”

This is what Yahweh says,
the Holy One of Israel, who made him:
“Do you quiz me about things to come?
Do you boss me around
about my children and the work of my hands?{g}

It was my doing that the earth exists
and that people live on it.
My own hands spread out the sky,
and I gave orders to all its stars.

I have stirred up Cyrus to do what is right,
and I will clear every road for him.
He will rebuild my city
and let my exiles go free.
He will not do it for payment or a gift,”
says Yahweh of Armies.

This is what Yahweh says:
“The goods of Egypt and the profits of Cush,
and the Sabeans, those tall men,
will cross over to you and become yours.
They will follow behind you.
They will cross over in chains
and bow down to you.
They will plead with you,
‘God is surely with you, and there is no other.
There is no other god.’”{h}

Truly you are a God who hides,
the God of Israel, who rescues.{i}

All of them will be shamed and disgraced.
Idol makers will go off together in confusion.

But Yahweh will save Israel
with a rescue that lasts forever.
You will never be shamed or disgraced,
for all time.

For this is what Yahweh says,
who created the sky (he is God!),
who shaped the earth and set it firmly in place
(he did not make it a wasteland,
but formed it as a home for people):
“I am Yahweh, and no one else is.{j}

I did not whisper in some hidden place,
in a dark corner of the earth.
I never told the children of Jacob,
‘Look for me in a wasteland.’
I, Yahweh, speak what is true.
I announce what is right.{k}

Gather and come near, you survivors of the nations!
People who carry their wooden idols around
and keep praying to a god that cannot save
know nothing.

Speak up and present your case.
Yes, let them put their heads together!
Who predicted this long ago?
Who foretold it ages back?
Was it not I, Yahweh?
No other god exists besides me,
a just God and a Savior.
There is no one but me.

Turn to me and be rescued,
all you at the ends of the earth.
For I am God, and there is no other.

I have sworn by my own name.
A true word has gone out of my mouth,
