and it will not be recalled:
‘Every knee will bend to me.
Every tongue will pledge loyalty to me.’{l}

They will say of me, ‘Only in Yahweh
are there victory and strength.’
All who were angry at him
will come to him and be ashamed.{m}

In Yahweh all of Israel’s descendants
will be made right and will boast.”

notes.text: Cyrus II ruled Persia from about 559 to 530 BC and took Babylon in 539 BC. “Anointed” is Hebrew mashiach (“Messiah”), a person chosen for a task. “Strip kings of their belts” means to take away their strength.
The Great Isaiah Scroll reads “the swelling places” (or “the rough places”) for “mountains.” The Septuagint says “I will make the rough places smooth.”
“Honored title” is Hebrew “I give you a surname.” Here it means “my anointed.”
Hebrew shalom (“peace”) and ra’ (“evil”), here “disaster.”
Hebrew tsedeq, “justice” or “righteousness.” The Hebrew word yesha’ means “rescue” or “salvation.”
Hebrew “a clay piece among the clay pieces of the earth.” Compare Romans 9:20-21.
The Hebrew of verse 11 is hard. Some read “Ask me about the things to come.”
Cush was south of Egypt. Sabeans came from Sheba, in southern Arabia or East Africa. Paul seems to echo verse 23 in Romans 14:11 and Philippians 2:10-11.
Or “God who hides himself” means “a God who keeps himself out of sight.”
Hebrew tohu, “empty,” as in Genesis 1:2.
Hebrew “I speak righteousness, I announce what is straight.”
Paul quotes verse 23 in Romans 14:11 and Philippians 2:10-11.
Or “In Yahweh alone, people will say to me, are victory and strength.” The Hebrew of this line is uncertain.

subheads.18: Turn to Me and Be Saved

verses.text:
Bel bows down. Nebo crouches.
Their idols are loaded onto animals and cattle.
The statues you used to carry in parades
are now a heavy burden for tired animals.{a}

“Listen to me, house of Jacob,
and every survivor of Israel’s family.
I have carried you from your birth.
I have held you from before you were born.

Until you are old, I stay the same.
Until your hair is gray, I will bear your weight.
I made you, so I will lift you up.
I will carry you and rescue you.{c}

Who will you compare me to, and treat as my equal?
Who will you match with me, so we can be alike?

Some pour gold out of their purses
and weigh silver on scales.
They pay a goldsmith to turn it into a god,
and then they kneel and worship it.

They hoist it to their shoulders and haul it away.
They set it in its spot, and it just stays there.
It will not budge.
Even if someone shouts to it, it will not answer.
It cannot pull anyone out of trouble.

Remember this and be firm.
Think about it again, you rebels.{d}

Remember what happened long ago.
I am God, and there is no other.
I am God, and there is none like me.

I tell the end from the beginning,
and long before it happens, what has not yet been done.
I say, ‘My plan will stand,
and I will do whatever I want.’{e}

I summon a hawk from the east,
a man from a distant land to carry out my plan.
I have spoken, and I will see it through.
I have designed it, and I will carry it out.{f}

You hard-hearted people, listen to me,
you who are far from doing what is right.

I am bringing my right way near. It is not far away,
and my rescue will not be late.
I will give rescue to Zion
and my glory to Israel.”{g}

notes.text: Bel (“lord”) was another name for Marduk, the chief god of Babylon. Nebo (Nabu) was his son, god of writing. The statues were carried in the New Year festival.
Some ancient copies read a little differently.
Hebrew “I will carry, and I will bear, and I will save.”
The Hebrew word for “be firm” is uncertain. It may mean “show yourselves to be men.”
Hebrew “my counsel will stand.”
The “bird of prey” is Cyrus of Persia. Compare 41:2 and 44:28.
Hebrew tsedaqah (“righteousness”) and teshu’ah (“salvation”). The Great Isaiah Scroll differs slightly.

verses.text:
“Come down and sit in the dust,
young Babylon, daughter of the Chaldeans.{a}
Sit on the ground, with no throne.
No one will call you
soft and pampered anymore.

Take the millstones and grind flour.
Take off your veil.
Pull up your skirt and bare your legs,
and wade through the rivers.{b}

Your body will be uncovered.
Your shame will be seen.
I will take revenge,
and I will not spare anyone.”{c}

Our Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
His name is Yahweh of Armies.

“Sit in silence and go into the dark,
daughter of the Chaldeans.
No one will call you
the queen of kingdoms again.

I was angry with my people.
I made my own family unholy,
and I gave them into your hands.
You showed them no mercy.
You laid a very heavy yoke even on the old.

So hear this, you who love pleasure,
you who sit safe in comfort,
who say to yourself,
‘I am the one, and no one else compares.
I will never end up a widow
or lose my children.’{e}

Both will come on you
in a moment, in one day:
the loss of children and being a widow.
They will fall on you with full force,
in spite of all your magic spells
and the great power of your charms.

You felt secure in your evil.
You said, ‘No one sees me.’
Your wisdom and knowledge led you off course,
and you told yourself,
‘I exist, and no one else does.’{f}

So disaster will come on you,
and you will not know how to stop it.
Trouble will fall on you
that you cannot buy off.
Ruin will hit you in a moment,
without any warning.{g}

Go on, then, with your spells
and your crowd of magic tricks,
which you have worked at since you were young.
Maybe they will do some good.
Maybe you can make people tremble.{h}

You are tired out by all your advisers.
Let them stand up and save you,
those who map the sky and watch the stars,
who announce month by month
what is coming on you.{i}

Look, they are like straw.
Fire burns them up.
They have no power to rescue themselves
from the flame.
This is no coal for warming yourself,
and no fire to sit beside!

That is what they will be to you,
the ones you worked with,
who traded with you since you were young.
Each one drifts off in his own direction.
No one is left to save you.”{j}

notes.text: “Young Babylon” is Hebrew “virgin daughter of Babylon,” a poetic name for the city. The Chaldeans were the people who ruled Babylonia.
Hebrew “pass through rivers.” Taking off the veil and skirt is a picture of a captive woman being led away.
The Hebrew of the last line is hard. It may mean “I will not meet a man” (that is, no one will help).
Hebrew “the end of it.”
Hebrew “I am, and there is no one besides me” is the same as the claim Yahweh makes in 45:5-6.
Some ancient copies read a little differently.
Hebrew “the dawn of it you will not know.”
Hebrew “your many sorceries.” The Hebrew can also be read “in which you have toiled.”
Hebrew “dividers of the sky” are astrologers.
Hebrew “no one saves you.”

verses.text:
Hear this, family of Jacob.
You carry the name Israel,
and you come from the line of Judah.
You swear by Yahweh’s name
and speak to the God of Israel,
but not with honesty or truth.{a}

You call yourselves people of the holy city
and lean on the God of Israel,
whose name is Yahweh of Armies.

“I announced the earlier events long ago.
They left my mouth, and I made them known.
Then I suddenly acted, and they happened.

I knew how stubborn you are,
that your neck is like an iron cord
and your forehead is like bronze.

So I told you ahead of time.
Before it happened, I let you hear it,
so you could never say, ‘My idol did this.
My carved statue and my metal image ordered it.’

You have heard it. Now look at all of it.
Will you not admit it?
From now on I am telling you new things,
hidden things you have never known.{b}

They are being made now, not ages ago.
Before today you had never heard of them,
so you cannot claim, ‘I knew all that.’

No, you never heard. No, you never knew.
No, your ear was never open long ago.
I knew how deceitful you would be,
and that you were called a rebel from birth.

For my name’s honor I am slow to get angry.
For my own praise I hold myself back from you,
so I will not wipe you out.

Look, I have refined you, though not the way silver is refined.
I have put you to the test in the furnace of pain.{c}

Hear me, Jacob,
and Israel, the one I summoned.
I am he. I am the first,
and I am the last as well.{e}

My own hand set the earth’s foundation,
and my right hand stretched out the sky.
When I call to them,
they all stand up together.

Gather, all of you, and listen.
Which of the idols announced these things?
The man Yahweh loves will do what Yahweh wants against Babylon,
and his arm will strike the Chaldeans.{f}

I, I have spoken. Yes, I have called him.
I have brought him, and his mission will succeed.

Come close and listen to this.
From the beginning I never spoke in secret.
From the moment it began, I was there.”
And now the Lord Yahweh has sent me, with his Spirit.{g}

Yahweh, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, says this:
“I am Yahweh your God.
I teach you what will benefit you.
I guide you down the road you must take.{h}

How I wish you had heeded my commands!
Then your peace would have been like a river,
and your right living like waves of the sea.

Your descendants would have been like sand,
and your children as many as its grains.
Their name would never be cut off
or wiped out in front of me.”

Leave Babylon! Run from the Chaldeans!
Announce it with a shout of joy.
Let everyone hear it. Carry the news to the far ends of the earth.
Say, “Yahweh has bought back his servant Jacob!”{i}
“There is no peace for wicked people,” says Yahweh.{k}

notes.text: Some ancient copies read a little differently. Some read “waters of” as “loins of.”
Or “hidden things you have not known.”
Or “I have chosen you in the furnace of suffering.”
Compare 42:8.
Compare Revelation 1:17 and 22:13.
The man Yahweh loves is probably Cyrus of Persia. The Chaldeans were the rulers of Babylon.
The speaker in the last line may be the prophet, or Yahweh’s servant.
Or “who teaches you to profit.”
Hebrew ga’al (“buy back”), the work of a family redeemer.
Compare Exodus 17:6 and Numbers 20:11.
Compare 57:21.

verses.text:
Listen to me, you islands.
Pay attention, you peoples far away.
Yahweh called me before I was born.
He spoke my name while I was in my mother’s body.{a}

He made my mouth like a sharp sword.
He hid me in the shadow of his hand.
He made me a polished arrow.
He kept me safe in his quiver.{b}

He said to me, “You are my servant,
Israel, the one by whom I will be honored.”{c}

But I said, “I have worked for nothing.
I spent my strength for emptiness and air.
Yet what is right for me is in Yahweh’s hands,
and my pay is with my God.”{d}

He says, “It is too small a job for you to be my servant,
only to raise up the tribes of Jacob
and bring home the survivors of Israel.
I will also make you a light for the nations,
so my rescue may reach the far ends of the earth.”{f}

This is what Yahweh says,
the Redeemer of Israel and his Holy One,
to the one people despise, whom nations hate,
the servant of rulers:
“Kings will see you and rise to their feet.
Princes will bow low.
They will do it because of Yahweh, who is faithful,
the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen you.”{g}

This is what Yahweh says:
“At the right time I answered you.
On the day of rescue I helped you.
I will protect you and make you a promise to the people,
to rebuild the land
and hand out the ruined properties again.{h}

You will tell prisoners, ‘Come out!’
and those in the dark, ‘Show yourselves!’
They will feed beside the roads
and find grass on every bare hill.

They will not go hungry or thirsty.
Scorching heat and sun will not hit them.
The one who pities them will lead them,
and take them to springs of water.{i}

I will turn all my mountains into roads,
and my highways will be built up.

Shout for joy, heavens! Cheer, earth!
Mountains, burst into song!
Yahweh is comforting his people
and will have pity on his suffering ones.

But Zion said, “Yahweh has left me.
The Lord has forgotten me.”

Can a mother forget her nursing baby
or have no pity on the child she bore?
Even if she could forget,
I will not forget you.

Look, I have carved you into my palms.
Your walls are always in front of me.{k}

Your children are hurrying back.
Those who tore you down and ruined you are leaving.{l}

Lift your eyes and look around.
All of them are gathering and coming to you.
As surely as I live, says Yahweh,
you will wear them all like jewels
and tie them on like a bride.

Your wrecked and empty places,
your land that was ruined,
will soon be too small for the people living in it,
and those who swallowed you up will be far away.

The children you had after your loss will say
so you can hear,
“This place is too crowded for me.
Move over so I can live here.”{m}

Then you will ask yourself,
“Who gave me these children?
I had lost mine and could not have more.
I was an exile, pushed around.
Who raised these?
I was left all alone.
So where did these come from?”

This is what the Lord Yahweh says:
“Watch, I will lift my hand toward the nations
and raise my flag for the peoples.
They will carry your sons in their arms,
and your daughters will ride on their shoulders.{n}

Kings will raise your children,
and their queens will nurse them.
They will bow to the ground in front of you
and lick the dust off your feet.
Then you will know that I am Yahweh.
No one who waits for me will be let down.”

Can a warrior’s loot be taken from him,
or a tyrant’s captives escape?{o}

But this is what Yahweh says:
“Even a warrior’s captives will be taken back,
and a tyrant’s loot will be rescued.
I will fight anyone who fights you,
and I will save your children.

I will make your oppressors eat their own flesh.
They will be drunk on their own blood, as on sweet wine.
Then everyone will know
that I, Yahweh, am your Savior,
and your Redeemer, the Strong One of Jacob.”{p}

notes.text: Compare Jeremiah 1:5 and Galatians 1:15.
The “servant” here is called Israel in verse 3. In verse 5 the servant seems to have a task for Israel. This is a hard passage.
Some ancient copies leave out “Israel.” The meaning of “show my glory” can also be “be glorified.”
Hebrew “my justice is with Yahweh, my wages with my God.”
Hebrew “and I am honored” (or “and let me be honored”).
Paul and Barnabas quote the end of verse 6 in Acts 13:47. Hebrew “my salvation.”
Hebrew “the despised of soul.”
Paul quotes the first part of verse 8 in 2 Corinthians 6:2. “Make a promise to the people” is Hebrew “make you a covenant for the people.”
Compare Revelation 7:16-17.
Sinim is an unknown place. It may be Aswan in Egypt, or a far-off land such as China. The Great Isaiah Scroll says “Syene.”
Hebrew “I have engraved you on the palms.”
The Great Isaiah Scroll and Septuagint read “your builders” for “your sons.”
Hebrew “the children of your bereavement.”
Hebrew “in the lap” for “in their arms.”
The Hebrew text says “a righteous man’s captives” but the Great Isaiah Scroll, the Septuagint, and other versions read “a tyrant’s captives.”
“Strong One of Jacob” is Hebrew ‘avir Ya’aqov. Compare 1:24 and Genesis 49:24.

verses.text:
This is what Yahweh says:
“Where is the divorce paper
that sent your mother away?
Or which of my creditors
took you as payment for a debt?
Look, you were sold because of your own sins,
and your mother was sent away because of your rebellion.{a}

When I came, why was nobody there?
When I called, why did nobody answer?
Is my hand too short to buy you back?
Do I lack the power to rescue?
With one shout I dry up the sea
and turn rivers into desert.
The fish rot for lack of water
and die of thirst.{b}

I dress the sky in black
and cover it with sackcloth.”

The Lord Yahweh has given me
the tongue of a student,
so I would know how to lift up the tired
with a word.
Every morning he wakes me.
He wakes my ear
to listen like a student.{c}

The Lord Yahweh opened my ear,
and I did not rebel.
I did not back away.

I offered my back to those who hit me
and my cheeks to those who yanked out my beard.
I did not cover my face
against insults and spit.{d}

But the Lord Yahweh helps me.
So I will not be disgraced.
That is why my face is set like flint,
and I am sure I will not be put to shame.{e}

Look, the Lord Yahweh helps me.
Who will say I am guilty?
Look, all of them will wear out like old clothes.
Moths will eat them up.

Who among you fears Yahweh
and listens to the voice of his servant?
Whoever walks in the dark
with no light at all,
let that person trust in Yahweh’s name
and lean on his God.{g}

Look, all of you who light fires
and arm yourselves with burning sticks,
go ahead, walk in the glow of your fire
and among the torches you lit!
This is what you will get from my hand:
you will lie down in pain.

notes.text: Hebrew “certificate of cutting off.” A “creditor” is a lender who could sell a debtor’s children as slaves (2 Kings 4:1).
Some ancient copies read a little differently.
Hebrew “the tongue of the taught ones.”
Hebrew “to those who tore out the beard.” Plucking a beard was a deep insult.
Hebrew “flint,” a very hard stone. Compare Luke 9:51 and Ezekiel 3:8-9.
Hebrew “the one who declares me right.” Compare Romans 8:33-34.
Hebrew “servant” (‘avdo).

verses.text:
“Listen to me, you who chase after what is right,
you who look for Yahweh.
Look at the rock you were cut from,
and the pit you were dug from.{a}

Think of Abraham, your ancestor,
and Sarah, who bore your people.
I called him when he was just one man,
and I blessed him and made his family large.{b}

For Yahweh has comforted Zion.
He has comforted all her ruins.
He will make her wasteland like Eden,
her desert like Yahweh’s garden.
Joy and gladness will live in her,
with thanks and the sound of singing.{c}

Hear me, my people.
Give ear, my nation.
Teaching will go out from me,
and I will make my justice a light to the peoples.{d}

My right way is near.
My rescue is on its way.
My arms will judge the peoples.
The islands wait for me,
and they hope in my arm.{e}

Lift your eyes to the sky
and look at the ground beneath you.
The sky will vanish like smoke.
The earth will wear out like a coat.
Its people will die like gnats.
But my rescue will last forever,
and my right way will never end.{f}

Listen to me, you who know what is right,
you people with my teaching in your hearts.
Do not be afraid of mortals’ scorn
or terrified by their insults.

The moth will eat them like a coat,
and the worm will eat them like wool.
But my right way will last forever,
and my rescue for all generations.”{g}

Wake up, wake up, put on strength,
arm of Yahweh!
Wake up as in the days of old,
the ages long ago!
Are you not the one who cut Rahab to pieces
and pierced the sea dragon?{h}

Was it not you who dried the sea up,
the waters of the great deep?
You made a road across the ocean floor
for the redeemed to cross.{i}

Those Yahweh bought back will return
and enter Zion with singing.
Joy that never ends will crown their heads.
Gladness and joy will catch them,
and sorrow and sighing will run away.{j}

and to forget Yahweh your Maker,
who stretched out the sky
and laid the earth’s foundation?
Why live in terror all day long
of the oppressor’s fury,
as if he were ready to destroy?
Where is the oppressor’s fury now?

I have put my words in your mouth
and sheltered you under my hand.
I did this so that I could set up the sky, lay the earth’s foundation,
and tell Zion, ‘You are my people.’”{n}

Rise up, rise up!
Stand up, Jerusalem.
From Yahweh’s hand you have drunk
the cup of his anger.
You downed the bowl, the cup that sends people reeling,
and you drained it dry.{o}

Of all the children she bore,
not one guides her.
Of all the children she raised,
not one takes her hand.

Two disasters have struck you.
Who will cry with you?
Ruin and destruction, hunger and the sword.
Who can comfort you?{p}

Your sons have collapsed.
They lie at the head of every street
like an antelope in a net.
They are full of Yahweh’s anger,
the rebuke of your God.{q}

So hear this, you who suffer,
you who are drunk, but not from wine.

This is what your Lord Yahweh says,
your God, who argues the case for his people:
“Look, I have taken the cup that made you stagger out of your hand,
the bowl of my anger. You will never drink from it again.{r}

I will place it in the hands of those who tormented you,
who told you,
‘Lie down so we can walk over you.’
You flattened your back like the ground,
a road for them to cross.”{s}

notes.text: “Rock” and “pit” mean the ancestors. See verse 2.
Abraham means “father of many.” Sarah means “princess.” Compare Genesis 12 and 15.
Eden means “delight.” Compare Genesis 2:8 and Ezekiel 36:35.
Or “instruction” (Hebrew torah).
Hebrew “islands” or “coastlands.” “Arms” is plural in the Hebrew.
Or “like gnats” or “in the same way.” The Hebrew can mean “die the same way.”
Some ancient copies read a little differently.
Rahab is a name for a sea monster in old stories (see Job 26:12 and Psalm 89:10). Here it may stand for Egypt. The “sea dragon” is Hebrew tannin.
Compare Exodus 14:21-22.
This verse is almost the same as 35:10.
Hebrew “a son of a man who is given up as grass.”
The Hebrew word for “pit” is shachat. Some ancient copies read a little differently.
Compare Jeremiah 31:35.
The Hebrew of the third line is “to plant the heavens” (or “to stretch out”).
Hebrew “cup of staggering.”
The Great Isaiah Scroll reads “who can comfort you” for “how can I comfort you.” Hebrew “Who will mourn?”
Hebrew to’; the animal is uncertain. It may be an antelope or an oryx.
Hebrew “cup of staggering.”
Compare Joshua 10:24.

subheads.12: I Am the One Who Comforts You

verses.text:
Wake up, wake up, Zion!
Put on your strength.
Dress in your finest clothes, Jerusalem, holy city.
Outsiders who are not clean will never walk through you again.

Shake off the dust and rise.
Take your seat, Jerusalem.
Free your neck from its chains,
captive Daughter Zion.{a}

This is what Yahweh says: “You were sold for nothing,
and you will be bought back without money.”
This is what the Lord Yahweh says: “In the beginning my people went down into Egypt and stayed there as outsiders. Then Assyria bullied them for no reason at all.
So what is going on here?” asks Yahweh. “Free of charge, my people were carried off. Their masters mock them,” says Yahweh, “and every day my name is slandered.{b}
Because of this, my people will come to know who I am. When that day comes, they will know that the one speaking is me. Here I am.”

How lovely on the hills
are the feet of the runner
carrying good news,
calling out peace and bringing word of happiness,
calling out rescue,
saying to Zion, “Your God rules as king!”{c}

Listen! Your sentries raise their voices.
They shout for joy as one.
Right before their eyes
they watch Yahweh return to Zion.

Break into song together,
ruins of Jerusalem!
Yahweh has comforted his people.
He has bought Jerusalem back.

Yahweh has rolled up his sleeve to show his holy arm
while every nation looks on.
The ends of the earth
will witness our God’s victory.

Out, out! Walk away from there!
Touch no unclean thing.
Leave her midst and keep clean,
you who carry the holy things of Yahweh.{d}

You will not leave in a rush
or run away in a panic.
Yahweh will walk in front of you,
and the God of Israel will guard your back.

Many were shocked at the sight of him.
His face was so marred he hardly looked human,
and his body hardly looked like a man’s.

In this way he will make many nations jump,
and kings will keep silent because of him.
They will see what nobody told them,
and grasp what they never heard.”{f}

notes.text: Hebrew shevi can mean “sit” or, with other vowels, “captive.”
Hebrew can mean “wail” or “boast.”
Paul quotes the first part in Romans 10:15. Compare Nahum 1:15.
That is, the temple tools. Compare Ezra 1:7-11.
Or “act wisely.” This is the start of the fourth song about the servant, which goes through 53:12.
Paul quotes this in Romans 15:21. Hebrew yazzeh, “sprinkle,” is also used for “startle” here. Some translators read it as “startle” and some as “sprinkle.”

subheads.13: The Servant Will Be Lifted High

verses.text:
Who believed what we heard?{a}
To whom did Yahweh show his mighty arm?

He grew up in front of him like a tender plant,
like a root in dry ground.
He had no royal look to make us stare,
nothing in his face to make us want him.

People looked down on him and turned him away.{b}
He was a man of sorrows who knew sickness.
Like someone people hide their faces from,
he was scorned, and we paid him no mind.

Yet it was our sicknesses he took up
and our sorrows he carried.
We assumed God had struck him down,
beaten him and made him suffer.{c}

But our rebellions are why he was stabbed,
and our sins are why he was crushed.
The beating that brought us peace landed on him,
and his bruises heal us.

We all wandered off like sheep.
Each of us went his own way.
And Yahweh laid on him
the sin of us all.

He was beaten down and he suffered,
but he never opened his mouth.
Like a lamb led off to be killed,
like a sheep silent in front of the people cutting its wool,
he never opened his mouth.{d}

After an unfair trial he was taken away.{e}
Who among his generation cared
that he was cut off from the land of the living,
hit for the rebellion of my people?

They gave him a grave with wicked men,
and a tomb with a rich man,
though he never did any violence,
and no lie was ever in his mouth.

But it was Yahweh’s plan to crush him with pain.
When he makes his life a payment for sin,{f}
he will see his children and live a long life,
and Yahweh’s plan will succeed through him.

After his deep suffering he will see light{g}
and be satisfied.
By knowing him, my good servant
will set many people right,
and he will carry their guilt.

For this I will assign him a share with important people,
and he will divide plunder with the mighty.
He emptied out his life, even to death,
and was listed among lawbreakers.
Still, he took the sin of many on himself
and stood up for the rebels.

notes.text: Or “our message.” John 12:38 and Romans 10:16 quote this.
Or “rejected.” Hebrew is uncertain.
Matthew 8:17 applies this to Jesus’ healings.
Acts 8:32-33 quotes verses 7-8 from the Greek Old Testament.
Hebrew is hard here. It can also mean “from prison and judgment.”
Hebrew asham, a guilt offering.
“Light” is in some ancient copies and the Greek Old Testament. The standard Hebrew text leaves it out.

verses.text:
“Sing, woman with no children!
Burst into song and shout for joy, you who never went through labor!
The deserted woman will have a bigger family
than the one with a husband,” says Yahweh.{a}

“Make more room for your tent.
Spread wide the curtains of your home, and do not skimp.
Make your ropes longer
and your pegs stronger.

You will burst out on the right and on the left.
Your descendants will take over other nations
and live in towns that were deserted.

Fear nothing, for you will not be shamed.
Do not lose heart, for no one will disgrace you.
The shame of your youth will slip from your mind,
and you will not recall the sorrow of your widowhood.

Your Maker is your husband.{b}
Yahweh of Armies is his name.
The Holy One of Israel is your Redeemer.
He is known as God of every land on earth.

Yahweh called you back,
like a wife deserted and grieving,
a bride from youth whom her husband threw out,” says your God.

“For one brief moment I abandoned you,
but with deep tenderness I will gather you.

In a burst of rage
I turned my face from you for a moment.
But I will show you kindness that never ends,”
says Yahweh, your Redeemer.

“For me this is like the days of Noah.
I made a promise then
that Noah’s flood would never again cover the land.
So now I promise
not to be furious with you or to scold you.

Mountains may be moved
and hills may totter,
but my faithful love will not leave you,
and my peace promise will not totter,”
says Yahweh, who has compassion on you.

Yahweh will teach all your children,{f}
and your children will have great peace.

You will stand firm in what is right.
Cruelty will be far from you, so you have nothing to dread.
Terror will stay away and will not come close.

If anyone stirs up trouble, I did not send it.
Anyone who attacks you will go down before you.

Look, I made the blacksmith
who blows on the coals
and makes a tool for his work.
And I made the destroyer who wrecks things.

No weapon made against you will win.
You will prove wrong every tongue that accuses you.
This is what Yahweh’s servants receive.
Their victory comes from me,” says Yahweh.

notes.text: Paul quotes this in Galatians 4:27.
The Hebrew word for “husband” is plural, a way to show greatness.
Hebrew puk, a dark paste used as eye makeup. Here it is a mortar that makes the stones stand out.
Or “lapis lazuli.” Compare Revelation 21:18-21.
The exact stones are uncertain.
Jesus quotes this in John 6:45.

verses.text:
“All who are thirsty, come to the waters!
Even if you have no money, come, buy and eat!
Come and buy wine and milk
with no money and no price.

Why pay for what is not food,
and work hard for what never fills you?
Listen carefully to me and eat well,
and your soul will enjoy the best of meals.

Turn your ear toward me and come.
Listen, and your soul will live.
Between us I will set up a covenant that never ends,
the steady love I promised to David.{a}

See, I made him a witness for the peoples,
a ruler and leader of nations.

You will summon nations you never knew,
and peoples who never knew you will rush to you.
It will be because of Yahweh your God, the Holy One of Israel,
who has made you beautiful.”

Look for Yahweh while he can be found.
Call to him while he is close.

Let the wicked give up their ways
and the evil their thoughts.
Let them come back to Yahweh, and he will have pity on them.
Let them come to our God, for he forgives freely.

“My thoughts are not your thoughts,
and your ways are not my ways,” says Yahweh.

“The sky is higher than the earth,
and so my ways are higher than yours,
my thoughts above your thoughts.

Just as rain and snow come down from the sky
and never go back up,
but soak the ground and make it grow and sprout,
giving seed to the planter and bread to the hungry,

So it is with my word that leaves my mouth.
It will not come back to me with nothing done.
It will accomplish what I wish,
and succeed in the mission I gave it.

Yes, you will leave in gladness
and be led out in peace.
Mountains and hills in front of you will break out in song,
and every tree of the field will applaud.

A cypress will grow where the thorns were.
A myrtle will grow where the weeds were.
This will make Yahweh famous,
a sign that lasts forever and is never erased.”

notes.text: Compare 2 Samuel 7 and Psalm 89.

verses.text:
This is what Yahweh says:
“Be fair and do what is right.
My rescue is about to come,
and my goodness is about to be shown.

Happy is the person who lives this way,
who holds on to it,
who keeps the Sabbath and does not treat it as common,
and who stops his hand from doing wrong.”

No foreigner who has joined Yahweh should think,
“Yahweh will surely shut me out of his people.”
No eunuch should think,
“Look at me. I am a withered tree.”

This is what Yahweh says:
“Eunuchs who keep my Sabbaths,
choose what pleases me,
and hold tight to my covenant,

will get something from me inside my house and walls.{a}
It is better than sons or daughters.
I will give each one a name that lasts forever,
one that will never be erased.

Foreigners will join Yahweh to serve him,
love his name, and be his servants.
They will keep the Sabbath and not make it common,
and they will hold tight to my covenant.

I will lead these people to my holy mountain
and make them glad inside my house of prayer.
Their burnt offerings and sacrifices
will be welcome on my altar.
My house will be named a house of prayer
for every people.”{b}

The Lord Yahweh, who brings home the scattered people of Israel, announces:
“I will bring in still more people,
besides the ones already gathered.”

Come and eat, all you wild animals,
all you creatures of the forest!

They are greedy dogs
that never get enough.
These are the shepherds,
and they understand nothing.
They all go their own way,
every one after what he can get.

“Come on,” each one says, “let me fetch some wine,{e}
and we will fill up on beer.
Tomorrow will be like today,
only better.”

notes.text: Hebrew yad vashem, “a hand and a name.” It means a memorial.
Jesus quotes this in Mark 11:17 when he clears the temple.
Hebrew “watchman” is singular in the written text.
The Hebrew word is uncertain. It may mean “panting” or “raving.”
Hebrew yayin, “wine.” Hebrew shekar means a strong drink such as beer.

verses.text:
Good people die,
and no one thinks about it.
Faithful people are taken away,
and no one sees
that they are being spared from the evil to come.

“But you, come here,
you children of a fortune-teller,
you offspring of an unfaithful man and a woman who sold herself.

Whom do you think you are mocking?
Who gets your sneers
and your stuck-out tongue?
Are you not rebels’ children,
a family of liars?

You burn with desire among the oaks,{b}
under every leafy tree.
You kill your children in the ravines
and under the overhanging rocks.

Your share is with the smooth stones of the ravine.{c}
Those, those are your lot.
You poured out drinks for them
and brought them gifts of grain.
Do you think that will make me calm?

You made your bed
on a tall, high hill,
and you climbed up there
to offer sacrifices.

You put up your symbol
behind the door and its frame.
You left me and stripped off your covers.
You climbed in and made the bed wide.
You struck a deal with those you love in that bed,
and you looked at their nakedness.{d}

You went to the king{e} with olive oil
and used lots of perfume.
You sent your messengers far away.
You sank down as low as the grave.

Your long road wore you out,
but you never said, ‘It is hopeless.’
You found fresh strength,
so you did not give up.

“Who scared you so much that you lied,
forgot me,
and never gave me a thought?
Is it because I stayed silent so long
that you do not fear me?

I will tell about your good deeds,
and they will do you no good.

Go ahead and shout for help.
Let your heap of idols rescue you!
The wind will lift every one away.
One puff will blow them off.
But whoever runs to me for safety will inherit the land
and own my holy mountain.”

Someone will say,
“Build the road! Build it! Clear the way!{f}
Take every stumbling block
out of my people’s path.”

The high and lofty One, who lives forever and whose name is holy, speaks:
“I dwell on a high, holy height.
Yet I am also with the crushed and the humble.
I give new life to the humble
and new heart to the crushed.

I will not accuse forever,
and I will not stay angry for good.
If I did, people’s spirits would fail,
the very breath I made.

I was angry at their greedy sin.
I hit them and hid my face in rage.
But they kept on turning away,
following the path their hearts chose.

I have watched their conduct, yet I will heal them.
I will lead them and bring comfort back
to them and to their mourners.

I will create praise on their lips.
Peace, peace to those far off and those near,”
says Yahweh. “I will heal them.”

But wicked people are like the stormy sea,
which can never rest.
Its waves throw up mud and filth.
“The wicked will have no peace,” says my God.

notes.text: Or “each one who walked in his honesty.”
Or “among the great trees” or “among the gods.”
Hebrew has a word play on “smooth stones” and “your share.”
Hebrew “hand,” which may be a polite word for a private body part.
Hebrew melek, “king.” It may also be the god Molech. Compare Leviticus 18:21.
Compare 40:3 and 62:10.

verses.text:
“Shout as loud as you can. Do not hold back.
Make your voice sound like a trumpet.{a}
Confront my people with their rebellion,
and the family of Jacob with their sins.

They come looking for me day after day.
They claim they want to learn my ways,
like a people who did right
and never dropped their God’s rules.
They ask me for fair decisions
and say they love having God near.

They ask, ‘Why did we fast if you do not see it?
Why did we go without food if you did not notice?’
Look, on your fast day you do whatever you please
and push your workers hard.{b}

Look, your fasts end in fights and quarrels,
and in punching each other with wicked fists.
A fast like yours today
will never make your voice heard in heaven.

Is this the kind of fast I want,
a day when people go without food?
Is it bowing your head like a reed,
and lying down in rough cloth and ashes?
Do you call that a fast,
a day that pleases Yahweh?

“This is the fast I want:
to unlock the chains of injustice,
to loosen the straps of the yoke,
to set the oppressed free,{c}
and to break every yoke.

It is to share your food with hungry people,
to bring poor homeless people into your house,
to give clothes to someone you see without any,{d}
and not to hide from your own relatives.

Then your light will break out like sunrise,
and your healing will come fast.
Your goodness will walk ahead of you,
and Yahweh’s glory will protect your back.{e}

Then you will call out, and Yahweh will answer.
You will shout, and he will reply, ‘Here I am.’
Throw away the yoke among you,
the pointing finger, and the nasty talk.

Give your own food to the hungry
and meet the needs of people in trouble.
Then your light will dawn in the dark,
and your gloom will turn bright as noon.

Yahweh will always lead you.
He will fill you up in dry lands
and make your bones strong.
You will be like a well-watered yard,
like a spring that never fails.

Your people will rebuild the ancient ruins.
You will set up the foundations that stood for ages.
People will call you the one who fixes broken walls
and makes the streets fit to live on.

“Suppose you stop trampling the Sabbath
and doing what you like on my holy day.
Suppose you call the Sabbath a joy
and Yahweh’s holy day worthy of honor.
Suppose you honor it by not doing your own business,
not chasing your own fun, and not talking idly.

Then you will find joy in Yahweh.
I will make you ride over the high places of the land
and feed you from the inheritance of your ancestor Jacob.”
The mouth of Yahweh has spoken.

notes.text: Hebrew shofar, a ram’s horn.
Or “collect all your debts.”
Jesus reads a line like this in Luke 4:18.
The Great Isaiah Scroll adds “with a garment.”
Or “will be your rear guard.” Compare 52:12.

verses.text:
Look, Yahweh’s arm is not too short to rescue,
and his ear is not too dull to hear.

It is your sins that have built a wall
between you and your God.
Your wrongs have hidden his face from you,
so he does not listen.

Your hands are stained with blood,
and your fingers with guilt.
Your lips tell lies,
and your tongue mutters evil.

No one calls for fair treatment.
No one pleads a case in good faith.
They trust in empty words and tell lies.
They plan trouble and give birth to wrong.

They hatch snake eggs
and spin spider webs.
Whoever eats their eggs dies,
and when one is crushed, a viper hatches.

Their webs cannot become clothes,
and they cannot dress in what they make.
Their deeds are wicked deeds,
and their hands are full of violence.

Their feet rush toward evil,
and they hurry to spill blood of the innocent.
Their thoughts are wicked thoughts.
Ruin and wreckage mark their roads.

They do not know the road to peace,
and there is nothing fair along their paths.
They have made their roads twisted,
and no one who walks them finds peace.

This is why justice is far from us,
and what is right does not catch up with us.
We hope for light, but see only dark.
We hope for brightness, but walk in shadows.

We feel along the wall like blind people,
and grope around as if we had no eyes.
At midday we trip as though it were twilight.
Among the strong we look like dead men.

We all growl like bears
and moan like doves.
We look for justice, but find none.
Rescue, we hope, but it stays far away.

Our rebellions pile up in front of you,
and our sins speak against us.
Our rebellions are always with us,
and we know our guilt.

We have rebelled and lied about Yahweh.
We have turned away from our God.
We have talked of cruelty and treason,
saying lies our hearts made up.

Justice has been shoved back,
and what is right stands far away.
Truth has stumbled in the public square,
and honesty cannot get in.

Truth is missing,
and anyone who avoids evil is robbed.
Yahweh saw this, and he was displeased
that there was no justice.

He saw that no one would help.
He was shocked that no one stepped in.
So his own arm brought the rescue,
and his own goodness held him up.

He put on goodness like armor
and set the helmet of rescue on his head.{a}
He wore the clothes of payback
and wrapped himself in passion like a coat.

He will pay people back for what they did:
anger for his enemies and punishment for his foes.
He will repay even the far-off islands.

From the west people will fear the name of Yahweh,
and from the sunrise they will fear his glory.
He will surge in like a flooded river,
driven by the wind of Yahweh.{b}

“A Redeemer will come to Zion,
to those in Jacob who turn away from rebellion,” says Yahweh.{c}

“Here is my promise to them,” says Yahweh. “My Spirit is on you, and the words I put in your mouth will never leave your mouth. They will not leave the mouths of your children or grandchildren, from now on and forever,” says Yahweh.

notes.text: Compare Ephesians 6:14-17 and 1 Thessalonians 5:8.
Or “when the enemy comes like a river, Yahweh’s Spirit will raise a flag against him.”
Paul quotes verses 20-21 in Romans 11:26-27, close to the Greek Old Testament.

subheads.9: We Feel Our Way Like the Blind

verses.text:
Rise up and shine, for your light has come,
and Yahweh’s glory has dawned over you.

Darkness covers the earth,
and thick darkness covers the peoples.
But Yahweh dawns over you,
and his glory appears above you.

Nations will come to your light,
and kings to the bright sunrise over you.

Raise your eyes and look around.
Everyone is gathering. They are heading your way.
Your sons are coming from far off,
and your daughters are carried at the hip.{a}

Then you will see and beam with joy.
Your heart will race and swell,
because the wealth of the seas will be poured out for you,
and the riches of nations will arrive.

Camel herds will blanket your land,
young camels from Midian and Ephah.
Visitors from Sheba will all arrive
with gold and frankincense,
singing the praises of Yahweh.{b}

All the flocks of Kedar will be gathered to you.
The rams of Nebaioth will serve you.
They will go up on my altar and be welcome there,{c}
and I will make my beautiful house more beautiful still.

Who are these flying like clouds,
like doves heading for their nests?

The islands look to me,
and the big ships of Tarshish sail first.
They carry your children home from distant lands,
together with silver and gold,
to bring honor to the name of Yahweh your God,
the Holy One of Israel,
who has made you splendid.

Foreigners will build up your walls,
and their kings will work for you.
I struck you in my anger,
yet because I favor you I have shown pity.

Your gates will stand open all the time.
They will never be shut, day or night,
so people can bring you the riches of the nations,
with their kings leading the parade.{d}

Any nation or kingdom
that will not serve you will perish.
Nations like that will be totally destroyed.

The glory of Lebanon will come to you:
its cypress, fir and pine all together,
to decorate my holy place.
I will give honor to the place where my feet rest.

The children of those who beat you
will come to you bowing low.
Those who looked down on you will bend at your feet.
They will name you City of Yahweh,
Zion of the Holy One of Israel.

You were deserted and hated,
and no traveler came by.
But I will turn you into an everlasting pride,
a joy for every generation.

You will drink the milk of nations
and be nursed by royal breasts.
Then you will know that I, Yahweh, am your Savior,
your Redeemer, the Strong One of Jacob.

Where there was bronze I will bring gold.
Where there was iron I will bring silver.
Where there was wood I will bring bronze,
and iron where there were stones.
I will make peace your guard
and justice your boss.

No more violence will be heard in your land,
no more ruin or wreckage inside your borders.
You will call your walls Rescue
and your gates Praise.

The sun will not be your daylight anymore,
and the moon will not give you light at night.{e}
Yahweh will be your light that never ends,
and your God will be your glory.

Your sun will never set,
and your moon will never fade,
because Yahweh will be your light forever,
and your days of sadness will be over.

All your people will be good people.
They will own the land forever.
They are my own planting, my own handiwork,
and they will show how great I am.

The smallest family will grow into a thousand,
and the tiniest into a strong nation.
I am Yahweh. When the time comes, I will do it quickly.

notes.text: Hebrew “nursed on the side,” meaning carried at the side.
Compare Matthew 2:11.
The Hebrew of this line is hard. Some ancient copies read a little differently.
Compare Revelation 21:25-26.
Compare Revelation 21:23 and 22:5.

verses.text:
He sent me to give those who mourn in Zion
a crown instead of ashes,{d}
the oil of gladness instead of grief,
and a coat of praise instead of a heavy heart.
They will be called Great Oaks of Goodness,
planted by Yahweh to show his glory.

They will build the old ruins again.
They will fix places wrecked long ago.
They will restore the broken cities
that lay empty for many generations.

Outsiders will stand and feed your flocks.
Foreigners will work your fields and vineyards.

But you will be called Yahweh’s priests.{e}
People will name you servants of our God.
You will enjoy the riches of the nations,
and take pride in what they own.

Instead of shame you will get twice as much.
Instead of disgrace they will cheer about what they receive.
So in their land they will own double,
and lasting joy will be theirs.

“I, Yahweh, love fairness.
I hate stealing and wrong.
I will reward them truthfully
and make a lasting covenant with them.

Their children will be famous among the nations,
and their grandchildren among the peoples.
Everyone who sees them will agree
that they are a family Yahweh has blessed.”

I will celebrate greatly in Yahweh.
My whole being will cheer for my God.
He has dressed me in clothes of rescue
and wrapped me in a coat of goodness.
I look like a groom dressed as a priest,{f}
or a bride wearing her jewels.

As the soil makes its sprouts come up,
and a garden makes its seeds grow,
so the Lord Yahweh will make goodness and praise
grow in front of every nation.

notes.text: Jesus read the first lines in the synagogue in Luke 4:18-19.
Hebrew peqah-qoah, which means opening or release.
Jesus stopped reading before this line. Compare 34:8 and 63:4.
Hebrew has a word play between pe’er, “crown,” and efer, “ashes.”
Compare Exodus 19:6 and 1 Peter 2:9.
Hebrew “acts as priest with a headband.”

verses.text:
I cannot stay quiet because of Zion.
I cannot sit still because of Jerusalem,
until her goodness shines like sunrise
and her rescue burns like a torch.

Nations will watch your victory,
and all kings will see your glory.
You will get a new name
that Yahweh himself will give.{a}

You will be a beautiful crown in Yahweh’s hand,
a royal headband held by your God.

As a young man marries a young woman,
so your Builder will take you as his bride.{f}
As a groom is happy over his bride,
so your God will be happy over you.

I have set guards on your walls, Jerusalem.
They will not be quiet
for a single day or night.
You who call Yahweh to remember,
take no rest.

Give him no rest
until he makes Jerusalem strong
and the praise of the whole earth.

Yahweh has made a vow, swearing by his right hand
and his mighty arm:
“No more will your grain go
to your enemies as food.
Foreigners will not drink the new wine
you worked so hard to make.

Whoever harvests the grain will eat it
and praise Yahweh.
Whoever picks the grapes will drink the wine
in my holy place’s courtyards.”

Go out, go out through the gates!
Prepare the road for the people.
Build up the highway and throw out the stones.
Raise a flag for the nations.{g}

Look, Yahweh has announced
to the far ends of the earth:
“Tell the daughter of Zion,
‘See, your Savior is coming.{h}
His reward is with him,
and his payment goes in front of him.’”

They will be called the Holy People,
the Ones Yahweh Bought Back.
And you will be called Wanted,
the City That Is Never Left.

notes.text: Compare 65:15 and Revelation 2:17.
Hebrew Azuvah, “Forsaken.”
Hebrew Shemamah, “Desolate.”
Hebrew Hephzibah, which means “my delight is in her.” It was also the name of King Manasseh’s mother (2 Kings 21:1).
Hebrew Beulah, “married.”
Or “your sons will marry you.” The Hebrew can be read both ways.
Compare 57:14 and 40:3.
Compare 40:10. Matthew 21:5 mixes this with Zechariah 9:9.

verses.text:
Who is this coming from Edom,{a}
from Bozrah,{b} with clothes stained red?
He is dressed in splendor
and walks with great power.
“It is I, who speak of victory,
strong enough to rescue.”

Why are your clothes red,
like the clothes of someone stomping grapes?

“I stomped the grapes alone.
No one from the nations helped.
I trampled them in my anger
and crushed them in my rage.
Their blood spattered my clothes,
and stained all that I was wearing.{c}

I had planned a day of payback,
and the year to buy my people back had come.

I looked, and no one was there to help.
I was shocked that no one stepped in.
So my own arm won the victory for me,
and my rage held me up.

I stomped on nations in my anger.
In my rage I made them stagger,
and I poured their blood on the ground.”

I will speak of Yahweh’s faithful love
and the deeds that deserve praise,
all that Yahweh gave us,
and the many kind things he did
for the family of Israel
out of his pity and great love.

He said, “Surely they are my people,
children who will not cheat me.”
So he became their Savior.

When they suffered, he suffered too.{d}
The angel who stood before him saved them.
In his love and pity he bought them back.
He lifted them up and carried them
all through the days of old.

Yet they rebelled
and made his Holy Spirit sad.{e}
So he turned into their enemy
and fought against them himself.

Then they thought back to ancient times,
to Moses.{f}
Where is he who hauled them up out of the sea
along with the shepherds of his sheep?
Where is he who set his Holy Spirit
within their hearts,

who sent his glorious arm
to walk at Moses’ right hand,
who split the waters in front of them
to make himself a name that never dies,

who led them through the deep waters?
Like a horse running on open ground,
they did not trip.

Like cattle that walk down into a valley,
the Spirit of Yahweh gave them rest.
That is how you guided your people,
winning a glorious name for yourself.

Gaze down from heaven and see,
from your holy and beautiful home.
Where are your passion and your power?
Your deep feelings and pity
are held back from me.

You are our Father.
Abraham has no idea who we are,
and Israel does not know us.
You, Yahweh, are our Father.
Long ago you were named “Our Redeemer.”{g}

Yahweh, why do you let us drift from your paths
and make our hearts so hard that we stop fearing you?
Come back, for your servants’ sake,
for the tribes that belong to you.

Your holy people held your land for only a short time,{h}
and our enemies have trampled your holy place.

We have become like people you never ruled,
like people who never carried your name.{i}

notes.text: “Edom” sounds like the Hebrew word for “red.” Compare Genesis 25:30. Revelation 19 uses a picture like this.
Bozrah was a main city of Edom. Its name sounds like the Hebrew for “grape harvest.”
Some ancient copies leave out part of this verse, perhaps because a copyist’s eye skipped ahead.
The Hebrew can also mean “In all their suffering he was not an enemy” or “he did not suffer.” The standard text has two readings.
Compare Ephesians 4:30.
Or “his people remembered the old days of Moses.”
Hebrew go’el, “redeemer.”
Or “held your holy place.”
In Hebrew, this verse goes on into the line English Bibles number 64:1.

subheads.11: Where Is the One Who Led Us?

verses.text:
How I wish you would rip open the sky and come down!
The mountains would shake in front of you,{a}

as when fire lights dry twigs
or makes water bubble.
Then your enemies would learn who you are,
and nations would shake at your coming!

You did stunning things we never saw coming.
You came down, and mountains trembled in your presence.{b}

You meet those who happily do right
and keep your ways in mind.
But you were angry, since we kept sinning.
We have been wrong for ages. Can we still be saved?{d}

We have all turned into something unclean,
and our best deeds are like filthy rags.{e}
We all dry up like leaves,
and our sins sweep us off like the wind.

Nobody prays to you.
Nobody makes an effort to cling to you.
You have turned your face away from us
and let our sins melt us.{f}

Do not stay angry with us forever, Yahweh.
Do not remember our sins always.
Please, take a look. All of us are your people.

Your holy towns are a desert.
Zion is a desert.
Jerusalem is a pile of ruins.

Our holy and beautiful temple,
the place where our ancestors sang your praise,
was burned down,
and all that we treasured lies in ruins.

With all this happening, Yahweh, will you hold back?
Will you stay quiet and keep punishing us?

notes.text: In the Hebrew Bible this verse is 63:19, and the numbers in chapter 64 run one ahead of English Bibles.
Some ancient copies leave out a phrase in this verse.
Paul echoes this in 1 Corinthians 2:9.
The Hebrew of the last line is unclear. The Greek Old Testament reads “so we strayed.”
Hebrew “a garment of a woman’s period,” meaning something ritually unclean (Leviticus 15:19-24).
Some ancient versions read “let us melt” instead of “let us rot.”
Compare Jeremiah 18:6 and Romans 9:20-21.

verses.text:
“I let myself be asked by people who never asked for me.
I let myself be found by people who never looked.
To a nation that did not use my name
I said, ‘Here I am, here I am.’{a}

All day long I have reached out my hands
to a stubborn people
who walk a bad road,
chasing their own ideas.{b}

They are a people who keep provoking me
to my very face,
making offerings in garden shrines
and burning incense on brick altars.{c}

They sit in graves
and spend nights in secret places.{d}
They eat pig meat,
and their bowls hold soup made from unclean food.

They say, ‘Stay back.
Do not come near me. I am holier than you.’{e}
These people are smoke in my nose,
a fire that burns all day.

Look, I have this written down before me.
I will not rest until I pay back.
I will pay back in full,

for your sins and also those of your ancestors,”
says Yahweh.
“They burned incense on the mountains
and mocked me on the hills.
So I will measure out their payment
for what they did first.”

This is what Yahweh says:
“When there is still juice in a bunch of grapes,
people say, ‘Do not ruin it.
There is something good in it.’
I will do the same for my servants’ sake.
I will not destroy them all.

I will bring a family out of Jacob,
and from Judah an heir to my mountains.
My chosen people will own the land,
and my servants will settle there.

“But you who leave Yahweh,
who forget my holy mountain,
who set out a table for Gad
and fill cups of mixed wine for Meni,{g}

I will hand you over to the sword,
and each of you will kneel down to be killed.
I called, and you did not answer.
I spoke, and you did not listen.
You did what I call evil,
and chose what I do not like.”

So the Lord Yahweh says this:
“See, my servants will eat,
but you will go hungry.
My servants will drink,
but you will go thirsty.
My servants will rejoice,
but you will be embarrassed.

My servants will sing with happy hearts,
but you will cry with aching hearts
and wail with broken spirits.

You will leave your name behind,
and my chosen ones will use it in curses.
The Lord Yahweh will put an end to you,
but he will give his servants another name.

Then anyone who asks for a blessing in the land
will ask the God of truth,{h}
and anyone who swears an oath in the land
will swear by the God of truth.
The old troubles will be forgotten
and hidden from my eyes.

“Look, I am making a new sky
and a new earth.{i}
The old things will not be remembered
or come to mind.

So be glad and celebrate forever
in what I make.
I am turning Jerusalem into joy,
and her people into delight.

I will celebrate over Jerusalem
and enjoy my people.
The sound of crying
and weeping will never be heard there again.{j}

No baby will live only a few days there.
No old person will die before life is full.
Dying at a hundred will count as dying young,
and anyone who dies before a hundred will seem cursed.{k}

Houses will be built, and the builders will live in them.
Vineyards will be planted, and the planters will eat their grapes.

Others will not move into houses my people build,
and others will not eat what my people plant.
My people will have days as many as a tree’s,
and my chosen ones will enjoy their handiwork for years.

They will not work for nothing,
or raise children for sudden disaster.
They are a family blessed by Yahweh,
and their children are blessed with them.

I will answer before they even call.
While they are still talking, I will listen.

Wolf and lamb will eat side by side.
The lion will eat straw like the ox,
and the snake will eat dust.
Nothing on all my holy mountain
will hurt or ruin anything,” says Yahweh.{l}

verses.text:
This is what Yahweh says:
“The sky is my throne,
and the earth is my footstool.
Could you possibly build me a house?
Where would my resting place be?{a}

My own hand made all of this,
and so it all came to be,”
says Yahweh.
“These are the people I notice:
the humble, the broken in spirit,
who shake when I speak.

But the one who kills a bull is like one who kills a person.
Someone who gives a lamb is like one who wrings a dog’s neck.
The one who brings grain is like one who offers pig’s blood.
The one who burns incense as a reminder is like one who blesses an idol.{b}

They have picked their own ways,
and they enjoy their disgusting habits.
So I will pick how to treat them harshly
and bring on them the very things they fear.
I called, and no one answered.
I spoke, and no one listened.
They did what I call evil
and chose what I do not like.”

Hear the word of Yahweh,
you who shake when he speaks:
“Your own people hate you
and throw you out because of my name.
They say, ‘Let Yahweh show his glory
so we can see you happy.’
But they will be the ones put to shame.

Hear it! A roar from the city!
A roar from the temple!
It is the voice of Yahweh
paying back his enemies.

“Before labor started,
she gave birth.
Before the pains came,
she delivered a son.{c}

Who ever heard of such a thing?
Who has ever seen the like?
Is it possible for a land to be born in a day?
Can a whole people appear at once?
Yet Zion had barely started labor
when she gave birth to her children.

Would I bring a baby to the point of birth and then not let it be born?”
asks Yahweh.
“Would I, who deliver babies, shut the womb?”
asks your God.

“Celebrate with Jerusalem and cheer for her,
all who love her.
Join her in her joy,
all who mourned over her.

You will drink deeply
from her comforting breast.
You will drink and be thrilled
by the flood of her glory.”{d}

This is what Yahweh says:
“Look, I will send peace flowing to her like a river
and the riches of nations like a flood.
You will drink as a nursing child, be carried on her hip,
and rocked on her knees.

Just like a mother consoling her child,
I will console you.
In Jerusalem you will find comfort.

When you see this, your hearts will be glad,
and your bones will flourish like fresh grass.
Yahweh’s hand will be known among his servants,
and his anger among his enemies.

Look, Yahweh is coming in fire.
His chariots are like a storm.
He will answer his anger with fury
and his warning with flames of fire.

“Some people make themselves holy and clean to enter the gardens,
walking behind the one in the center.{f}
They eat pig meat, disgusting creatures and mice.
They will all come to an end together,” says Yahweh.

I will set a sign among them.
I will send some of the survivors to far-off lands:
to Tarshish, Pul and Lud, famous for their bows,{h}
to Tubal and Javan, and to distant islands
that have heard nothing about me and have not seen my glory.
They will tell of my glory to the nations.

From every nation they will bring all your relatives
as a gift to Yahweh.
They will come on horses and in chariots and wagons,
on mules and camels,
to my holy mountain, Jerusalem,” says Yahweh.
“They will come as Israelites bring grain offerings
in clean dishes to Yahweh’s house.

And I will pick some of them as well
to be priests and Levites,” says Yahweh.{i}

“Just as the new sky and new earth
that I am making
will last in front of me,” says Yahweh,
“so your children and your name will last.

Every month on the new moon
and every week on the Sabbath,
everyone will come to bow down to me,”
says Yahweh.

“They will go out and gaze
on the corpses of the people
who turned against me.
Their worm will not die,
their fire will not go out,
and everyone will be sickened by them.”{j}
